C-WL-001E.title_en: Seeking Truth from Facts — Anhui Rural Reform Direction Judgment Case
C-WL-001E.description_en: During the early reform and opening-up period, Wan Li, as a provincial party secretary in Anhui, insisted on judging policies based on actual rural conditions. He supported the Xiaogang Village contract responsibility practice, not deferring to established doctrines but focusing on whether farmers livelihoods actually improved.

C-WL-002E.title_en: Bold Exploration — Economic Special Zone Development Case
C-WL-002E.description_en: Wan Li actively supported the establishment of economic special zones in central leadership, advocating breakthrough beyond traditional planned economy constraints and bold exploration of market-oriented pathways.

C-WL-003E.description_en: Wan Li consistently used practical outcomes as the evaluation criterion: increased agricultural production, revitalized cities, and improved people livelihoods — all verified by actual development data.

C-WL-004E.title_en: Gradual and Prudent — Reform and Stability Balance Case
C-WL-004E.description_en: While advancing rural economic reform, Wan Li adhered to prudence: first piloting in Xiaogang Village and a few areas, then gradually expanding after successful results — promoting reform while maintaining social stability.

C-WL-005E.title_en: Merit-Based Personnel — Cadre System Reform Case
C-WL-005E.description_en: In central leadership positions, Wan Li vigorously promoted cadre system reform, advocating the abolition of seniority-based promotion and selection of young cadres based on merit regardless of background.

C-WL-006E.title_en: Investigation and Research — Economic Policy Formulation Case
C-WL-006E.description_en: While presiding over the State Council, Wan Li insisted on visiting various regions for field investigations, fully listening to grassroots opinions and obtaining first-hand data before formulating economic policies.

C-WL-007E.title_en: Key Breakthrough — Industrial Structure Adjustment Case
C-WL-007E.description_en: In State Council leadership, Wan Li focused on agriculture and energy as two key breakthrough areas while balancing the development of light industry and improvement of people livelihood.

C-WL-008E.title_en: Intra-Party Democracy — Major Decision Process Case
C-WL-008E.description_en: As Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, Wan Li vigorously promoted intra-party democracy and improvement of the people congress system, emphasizing collective discussion and broad consultation in decision-making.

C-WL-009E.title_en: Institutional Innovation — Rule of Law Construction Case
C-WL-009E.description_en: During his NPC work, Wan Li promoted important legislative and institutional reforms: improving the people congress system and strengthening socialist rule of law construction.

C-WL-010E.title_en: Historical Experience — Reform Process Summary Case
C-WL-010E.description_en: In his later years, Wan Li reviewed the reform and opening-up process, extracting valuable historical experiences from his participation in rural reform and special zone development to provide references for future reforms.

C-SY-E001.title_en: C-SY-E001: Wood Credibility — Establishing Government Trust
C-SY-E001.description_en: A new regime or reformer needs to establish legal authority among the people, proving government reliability through landmark events like the wood-moving reward.

C-SY-E002.description_en: Organize citizens into mutual monitoring groups, ensuring law enforcement efficiency through collective responsibility.

C-SY-E003.description_en: Establish a social mobility mechanism based on performance rather than bloodline, granting status and resources through military merit.

C-SY-E004.description_en: Abolish the old land system, allowing private ownership and free trade to release productive forces.

C-SY-E005.title_en: C-SY-E005: Agriculture-First Policy — Nation Built on Farming
C-SY-E005.description_en: Establish agriculture as the state foundation, concentrating resources for war preparation while suppressing commercial competition for agricultural labor.

C-SY-E006.description_en: Establish a unified national standard system, eliminating governance chaos caused by regional differences.

C-SY-E007.description_en: Strip noble hereditary privileges, establishing a social mobility mechanism based on performance rather than bloodline.

C-SY-E008.description_en: Consolidate small settlements into large counties, establishing a vertical management system for direct central rule over localities.

C-SY-E009.title_en: C-SY-E009: War-Preparation System — State through Warfare
C-SY-E009.description_en: Concentrate all national resources into agriculture and military cores, with territorial expansion as the sole path to state development.

C-SY-E010.title_en: C-SY-E010: Law Does Not Favor the Noble — Equality Before Law
C-SY-E010.description_en: Establish law without class distinction, applying punishment equally to ministers, generals and commoners.

C-SMQ-001E.description_en: Exploring the deep relationship between cosmic order (heaven) and human affairs. Sima Qian acknowledged both the existence of heavenly patterns and human agency, creating a dialectical historical ontology that transcends pure fatalism and pure humanism.
applications_en: Heaven-human relationship modeling in complex systems
Ecological ethics and sustainable development theory

C-SMQ-002E.description_en: 'Record the past to enlighten the future'—a practical historiography that serves as a wisdom repository for future statesmen. Sima Qian's work elevates history from passive recording to active political forecasting and governance guidance, demonstrating the practical relevance of historiography.

C-SMQ-003E.description_en: 'Straightforward words, verified facts; no false praise, no concealed evil'—the historiographical method prioritizing objective truth. After suffering castration as political persecution, Sima Qian maintained independent will to record historical truth faithfully. This method represents the highest moral standard and求真 will of a historian.

C-SMQ-004E.description_en: Distributing complex events of one figure across multiple chapters, creating multi-dimensional narrative through inter-chapter textual relationships. Xiang Yu's military achievements in his Basic Annals contrasted with Liu Bang's political maneuvering in his. This distributed narrative avoids the bias of a single perspective.

C-SMQ-005E.description_en: 'Grand Historian says'—independent commentary at the end of each chapter integrating narrative with value judgment. Through 'Grand Historian says', Sima Qian expressed political philosophy and value assessments beyond mere event summary. This method established the tradition of historiographical commentary.
applications_en: Independent analysis in policy evaluation reports

C-SMQ-006E.description_en: Pioneering five genres: basic annals, tables, treatises, hereditary houses, and biographies. By making character biographies the core of historical narrative—from emperors to warriors, assassins, merchants and scholars—Sima Qian gave all social strata a place in history writing. This broke the tradition of purely chronological arrangement.

C-SMQ-007E.description_en: Comparing the fates and choices of similar figures across different eras to extract historical patterns. Placing Chen Sheng in hereditary houses to affirm his founding contribution, or Bo Yi with Shu Qi to honor integrity. This method emphasizes trans-era historical similarities, discovering deep patterns rather than surface differences.

C-SMQ-008E.description_en: Transcending purely political and military narrative by incorporating culture, economy, and technology into historical writing. Treatise on Standardization (economy), Biographies of Wandering Knights (grassroots society), and Money-makers (commercial civilization) together form a multi-dimensional framework. This expanded history from emperors' solo to society's立体 painting.

C-SMQ-009E.description_en: 'Death is inevitable for all; some are heavier than Mount Tai, others lighter than a goose feather'—after suffering castration's humiliation, transforming individual suffering into historical responsibility and civilizational contribution. Sima Qian completed his monumental work through a historical mission transcending personal glory and shame, demonstrating the capacity to elevate individual suffering into cultural creation.
applications_en: Psychological transformation theory in adversity management

C-SMQ-010E.description_en: Acknowledging both cosmic order (disasters, omens) and human agency. Affirming grassroots revolution in Chen She's Basic Account while criticizing Xiang Yu's arrogance—reflecting a complex historical view transcending simple fatalism. This method preserves full space for human free will while acknowledging cosmic constraints.

C-GAN-001E.description_en: When the 1906 Transvaal Asiatic Registration Act forced Indians to register, Gandhi named his method satyagraha at a mass meeting: certificates were burned in public and thousands went to jail over eight years—voluntary suffering in place of obedience to an unjust law, until the 1913 miners' strike forced partial concessions.

C-GAN-002E.description_en: 1920-22: lawyers left courts, students left schools, titles returned, foreign cloth burned in the streets—colonial courts and markets visibly seized while the Congress became a mass organization of millions; vows and beating drills kept eight months of campaign from collapsing into riot.

C-GAN-003E.title_en: The 1932 Fast that Forced the Poona Pact
C-GAN-003E.description_en: Against the Communal Award's separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, Gandhi fasted to the edge of death—Hindu leaders and Ambedkar negotiated the Poona Pact that rewrote the electoral settlement; one act of self-suffering redrew a constitution.

tags_zh: 以对手升级为升级信号
C-GAN-004E.title_en: Twenty-One Latent Years in South Africa
C-GAN-004E.description_en: From the Natal Indian Congress and years of petitions logged in Indian Opinion to the first deliberate law-breaking only in 1906—twelve purely legal years banked cases, cadres, and reputation; back in India, Champaran, Ahmedabad, and Kheda re-ran the loop before the 1920 offensive.

C-GAN-005E.description_en: When demonstrators burned a police station and 22 officers died in 1922, Gandhi suspended the entire national movement within days and confessed responsibility publicly—accountability pointed inward, and the campaign switched from offensive to moral rebuilding rather than collapse.

C-GAN-006E.description_en: Gandhi renamed the Depressed Classes 'children of God,' lived in their villages, and fasted out the Poona Pact—pushing the front's entrance touchstone into constitutional revision; Hindu-Muslim unity and abolition of untouchability stood as the front's constitution, not its spoils.

C-GAN-007E.title_en: Khadi: Independence Cut into Half-Hours of Spinning
C-GAN-007E.description_en: Homespun became the material of uniform and flag; by 1940 Gandhi's ledger recorded 275,000 villagers earning Rs. 34.86 lakh through the wheel—participation at zero threshold, spending daily rather than rallying once, and the program reverse-engineered from the pain points of spinners and peasants.

C-GAN-008E.title_en: Village Republics: Independence as Accomplished Fact
C-GAN-008E.description_en: Panchayat-style bodies and khadi centers in thousands of villages meant the 1947 handover found no vacuum at the base—'expel the ruler, keep his machine, and you have only changed the operator' (Hind Swaraj) is the philosophical root making liberation constructive.

C-GAN-009E.title_en: The Salt March: Scale, Symbol, Absurdity
C-GAN-009E.description_en: A public letter announcing the crime, 385 kilometers of walking, one pinch of salt at Dandi triggering nationwide defiance—the monopoly everyone can break made the injustice graspable in three seconds, and the state's police against walkers became free advertising for the movement's narrative.

C-GAN-010E.title_en: My Experiments with Truth: A Life as Lab Log
C-GAN-010E.description_en: Gandhi titled his autobiography 'experiments with truth': dietary, celibacy, and silence trials with failures on record; after Amritsar he revised his stance on empire openly and late in life his views on caste and machinery—every reversal carried reasons and costs, iteration rather than collapse.

tags_en: Springbok Jersey: Symbol Reclamation in One Afternoon
C-MAN-001E.title_en: Springbok Jersey: Symbol Reclamation in One Afternoon
C-MAN-001E.description_en: 1995年橄榄球世界杯决赛，曼德拉身穿跳羚队6号皮纳尔球衣入场颁奖——跳羚曾是黑人受辱的符号，总统亲身穿用使白人球迷当场齐呼'曼德拉'：一个分裂图腾在90分钟内被重新赋义为全国团结的容器。

tags_en: The Government of National Unity: Real Power for the Defeated
C-MAN-002E.title_en: The Government of National Unity: Real Power for the Defeated
C-MAN-002E.description_en: 1994年首次不分种族普选后，曼德拉把刚被击败的国民党纳入内阁、党魁德克勒克出任第二副总统，并纳因卡塔入阁——胜利者在收编窗口期内给旧敌实权职位，把'再打下去也许能翻盘'从对手精英的工具箱里拿走，白人官僚与军警系统得以平稳过渡。

tags_en: One Term Only: Self-Weakening at the Peak
C-MAN-003E.title_en: One Term Only: Self-Weakening at the Peak
C-MAN-003E.description_en: 1999年曼德拉仅任一届总统即主动卸任、拒绝连任，公开自嘲'我不是圣人，除非你把圣人理解为不断尝试的罪人'——以卸任这一物理事实为'解放者不做终身执政'立下制度先例，卸任后又公开承认政府AIDS应对迟缓，把最大失分转为晚年公信力新支点。

tags_en: Nothing Over the People's Heads: Mandated Negotiation
C-MAN-004E.title_en: Nothing Over the People's Heads: Mandated Negotiation
C-MAN-004E.description_en: 1990-1994谈判期，曼德拉坚持一切重大让步'不得发生在人民头顶或背后'：谈判团队定期向群众大会汇报回炉、把反弹吸收为下一轮指令，1952年不服从运动锻造的十万会员与1994年普选（ANC约63%）一前一后为谈判装上授权的入口与出口钢印。

tags_en: The Island University: 27 Years as a Zero-Cost Investment
C-MAN-005E.title_en: The Island University: 27 Years as a Zero-Cost Investment
C-MAN-005E.description_en: 1962-1990年监禁期间，曼德拉把狱中时间记账为零机会成本投资期：在'罗本岛大学'修完伦敦大学校外学位、自学阿非利卡语并背诵其史诗，把囚禁本身经营成全球道德证词；1985年起更在狱中与司法部长科策开启'关于谈判的谈判'——蛰伏期内即铺好谈判轨道。

tags_en: Only Free Men Can Negotiate: Flipping the Frame
C-MAN-006E.title_en: Only Free Men Can Negotiate: Flipping the Frame
C-MAN-006E.description_en: 1985年博塔政府开出'放弃暴力换取释放'，接受即承认自己是被赦免的罪犯；曼德拉经律师转达'只有自由人才能谈判，囚徒签不了契约'——拒绝附条件善意、宁留狱中，并在1989年致博塔/德克勒克亲笔函中提出'先氛围后实质'两阶段框架，把议程设定权抓回手中。

tags_en: Truth for Amnesty: The TRC's Compelled Memory
C-MAN-007E.title_en: Truth for Amnesty: The TRC's Compelled Memory
C-MAN-007E.description_en: 1995-1998年真相与和解委员会（图图主持、曼德拉政治担保）以'完整公开陈述+政治动机证明=可申请赦免'运作：警察与安全官员公开陈述酷刑与处决细节，南非以两年听证换得别国靠审判也未必拿得到的完整命令链条——用司法确定性换档案完整性，把转型正义从复仇改写为疗愈。

tags_en: Demobilizing MK: The Verifiable De-escalation Signal
C-MAN-008E.title_en: Demobilizing MK: The Verifiable De-escalation Signal
C-MAN-008E.description_en: 1990年获释后，曼德拉顶住'人民战争'升级呼声，把武装行动的暂停与谈判进度挂钩——与1961年创立民族之矛时的公开宣言相对称，给德克勒克建制派以可采信的降级信号；谈判期间武装力量不解散、动员权不放弃，桌上每一分进展都有场外持续压力担保。

tags_en: Business First: Slicing the White Camp
C-MAN-009E.title_en: Business First: Slicing the White Camp
C-MAN-009E.description_en: 1990-1994年，曼德拉出狱数月内系统游说约翰内斯堡与伦敦商界，以市场、法治与稳定承诺使大企业与外国资本率先支持转型——商界换位大幅压低白人阵营抵抗收益；同时以'拒绝和谈'（而非身份）为唯一孤立标准，向军警承诺职业安全，数次极右翼哗变被建制派自身压下。

tags_en: The Rainbow Nation: Coexistence, Not Assimilation
C-MAN-010E.title_en: The Rainbow Nation: Coexistence, Not Assimilation
C-MAN-010E.description_en: 1994年就职演说与1996年宪法，曼德拉拒绝把新南非定义为'黑人夺回的国家'：以'彩虹之国'——多色并存而非熔成一色——为建国隐喻，以ubuntu'我在故我们在'为哲学底座，配以双声部国歌、六色新国旗等日常实物，使各群不必交出自己的历史即可共享国家；同时明示认同工程不替代经济再分配的未竟账目。

C-ASM-001E.title_zh: 制针厂：分工的第一台发动机
C-ASM-001E.description_zh: 《国富论》开篇场景（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-001E.title_en: The Pin Factory: Division of Labour as the First Engine of Wealth
C-ASM-001E.description_en: The opening scene of The Wealth of Nations (1776): one untrained workman performing all eighteen operations alone 'could scarce make one pin in a day, certainly not twenty'; but ten workers split among drawing, cutting, pointing, and heading 'upward of forty-eight thousand pins in a day.' Productivity is a function of structure, not the sum of diligence—division of labour is wealth's first engine, and its extent is limited by the size of the market.

C-ASM-002E.title_zh: 屠夫、酿酒师与面包师：看不见的手
C-ASM-002E.description_zh: 《国富论》第一篇第二章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-002E.title_en: The Butcher, the Brewer, and the Baker: The Invisible Hand
C-ASM-002E.description_en: Book I, ch.2 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest. We address ourselves not to their humanity but to their self-love.' Cooperation among strangers is rewritten from benevolence into mechanism: address self-love, let prices carry information—and the individual, 'led by an invisible hand,' promotes an end no part of his intention, provided the institutions of natural liberty stand.

C-ASM-003E.title_zh: 公正旁观者：心中的那个人
C-ASM-003E.description_zh: 《道德情操论》第三篇（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-003E.title_en: The Impartial Spectator: The Man Within
C-ASM-003E.description_en: Part III of The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759): 'When I endeavour to examine my own conduct, I divide myself into two persons—the examiner and judge, and the person whose conduct is examined.' Moral judgment runs on imaginative position-taking (sympathy) and matures by upgrading the partial spectator of one's circle into the abstract impartial one; yet the man within can be corrupted by admiring the rich and neglecting the poor—Smith's late-life addition of a whole chapter on that corruption.

C-ASM-004E.title_zh: 灯塔与收费公路：公共品的判据
C-ASM-004E.description_zh: 《国富论》第五篇（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-004E.title_en: Lighthouses and Toll Roads: The Test for Public Goods
C-ASM-004E.description_en: Book V of The Wealth of Nations (1776): the sovereign's duty covers works 'which could never repay the expense to any individual or small number of individuals'—lighthouses, roads, bridges, education—while toll roads and bridge dues should be recovered from those who use them. The boundary of the state is not a philosophical stance but a cost-recovery test, and even communalized works stay under efficiency audit; Coase's 1974 study of Britain's private lighthouses later sharpened the Smithian lesson to check institutional facts first.

C-ASM-005E.title_zh: 中华帝国与小指：思想实验的极限
C-ASM-005E.description_zh: 《道德情操论》第三篇第三章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-005E.title_en: The Earthquake in China and the Little Finger: The Limits of Sympathy
C-ASM-005E.description_en: Part III, ch.3 of The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759): 'Let us suppose the empire of China was suddenly swallowed by an earthquake; the man of humanity in Europe, who heard of it, would express much sorrow and pursue his business or pleasure as usual—yet if he were to lose his little finger tomorrow, he would not sleep tonight.' An extreme hypothetical strips the noise of custom and rhetoric, baring the real structure of moral intuition: action follows the tension between spectating one's own situation and imagining another's.

C-ASM-006E.title_zh: 富人之源：节俭而非挥霍
C-ASM-006E.description_zh: 《国富论》第二篇第三章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-006E.title_en: The Source of the Wealthy: Frugality, Not Profusion
C-ASM-006E.description_en: Book II, ch.3 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'Capitals are increased by the private frugality and good conduct of individuals, silently and gradually accumulated. It is this, not the profusion of government, which has brought nations from poverty to opulence.' The politician who would direct private capital assumes 'an authority which could safely be trusted to no council or senate whatever'; every prodigal act is a deduction from the public capital, and every frugal man a public benefactor.

C-ASM-007E.title_zh: 同业密谋：对游说的最早预警
C-ASM-007E.description_zh: 《国富论》第一篇第十章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-007E.title_en: The Conspiracy of the Same Trade: The First Warning against Lobbying
C-ASM-007E.description_en: Book I, ch.10 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.' Collusion is structural, not a moral defect, so the answer must be institutional; 'the proposal of any new law or regulation of commerce which comes from this order ought always to be listened to with great precaution, and never adopted till after long and careful examination'—the ancestor of antitrust and anti-lobbying discourse, to be read in both directions (masters' tacit combination to keep wages down included).

C-ASM-008E.title_zh: 水与钻石：价值悖论的双层拆分
C-ASM-008E.description_zh: 《国富论》第一篇第四章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-008E.title_en: Water and Diamond: Splitting the Value Paradox
C-ASM-008E.description_en: Book I, ch.4 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'The word value has two different meanings—value in use, and value in exchange. Water has the greatest value in use and scarce any in exchange; a diamond has scarce any value in use, and a great quantity of other goods may frequently be had in exchange for it.' Splitting the senses dissolves the ancient paradox, and Smith's first answer—'labour is the real measure of the exchangeable value of all commodities'—hands off unfinished business that Ricardo, the marginalists, and Marx each took up in turn.

C-ASM-009E.title_zh: 税收四则：量能、确定、便利、经济
C-ASM-009E.description_zh: 《国富论》第五篇第二编（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-009E.description_en: Book V of The Wealth of Nations (1776): the subjects should contribute 'in proportion to their respective abilities' (equality); 'the tax which each individual is bound to pay ought to be certain and not arbitrary' (certainty); payment 'ought to be convenient' (convenience); and every tax 'ought to be so contrived as to take out of the pockets of the people as little as possible over and above what it brings into the public treasury' (economy). Smith runs the four maxims against Britain's poll taxes and tithes—their regressivity and arbitrariness named point by point—and a tax 'not in itself very grievous' becomes oppressive 'by a very small degree of uncertainty.'

C-ASM-010E.title_zh: 自然自由体系：主权者只剩三件事
C-ASM-010E.description_zh: 《国富论》第四篇第九章（中文场景库对应条目）
C-ASM-010E.title_en: The System of Natural Liberty: Three Duties of the Sovereign
C-ASM-010E.description_en: Book IV, ch.9 of The Wealth of Nations (1776): 'All systems either of preference or of restraint being completely taken away, the obvious and simple system of natural liberty establishes itself of its own accord. Every man, so long as he does not violate the laws of justice, is left perfectly free to pursue his own interest his own way.' The sovereign is discharged from superintending private industry—its duty 'only of three kinds: defence, justice, and certain public works.' 'Peace, easy taxes, and a tolerable administration of justice' is the best recipe for national opulence; his proposed non-monopolizing empire appeared the same year as the Declaration of Independence.

C-SW-001E.title_en: Drilling the Court Ladies: Sunzi's Demonstration Before King Helü
C-SW-001E.description_en: Around 512 BC Sunzi presented his thirteen chapters to King Helü of Wu. Asked to test the art on women, he drilled 180 court ladies with the king's two favorite consorts as squad leaders: thrice-decreed orders met with laughter, and Sunzi ruled the officers' offense—beheading both consorts—after which the ranks held to perfection. The doctrine was proven before any war: victory rehearsed before the fighting began.

C-SW-002E.title_en: Presenting the Thirteen Chapters: the Price List of Victory
C-SW-002E.description_en: Recommended seven times by Wu Zixu, Sunzi gained audience with Helü and presented the Art of War—opening with 'war is the great matter of the state' and closing with 'no ruler raises arms in anger': violence as a tiered exception, from attacking stratagem through alliances to armies and city walls, with subduing the enemy without battle as the acme. The king made him a general.

C-SW-003E.title_en: Three Armies Harass Chu: Six Years of Intelligence Before the Blow
C-SW-003E.description_en: Wu Zixu's 'three-army harassment' rotated Wu's forces against Chu's borders—'when they sortie, we withdraw; when they return, we sortie'—for six years, mapping Chu's dispositions, exhausting its mobilization, and compiling the full intelligence picture (a venal chief minister, a lost commander, a resentful court). The ledger of 'know the enemy, know yourself' was written six years before Boju.

C-SW-004E.title_en: Landing at the Huai Mouth: Seizing When and Where
C-SW-004E.description_en: Before Boju (506 BC), Wu and Chu had long faced each other along the Huai with river fleets. The Wu army disembarked and crossed the three mountain passes into Chu's northeastern depths, pulling the battlefield off Chu's prepared river defenses—Chu had to fight at a time and place it never chose. The timetable of decision was written by Wu.

C-SW-005E.title_en: Piercing at Boju: the Thin Wall of a Crossing Army
C-SW-005E.description_en: The armies faced each other across the Han River. Chu's complacent chief minister led his main body across to fight before forming a proper line; Wu declined the fortified approaches and struck only the void—a crossing army, half in the water, unformed—at the single point of Boju. One point pierced, five battles won, the capital Ying taken in ten days.

C-SW-006E.title_en: Feigning Retreat at the Han: Reading the Scripted Form
C-SW-006E.description_en: During the Han River standoff Wu feigned withdrawal, showing 'inability' to lure Chu across the river; as the Chu line scattered mid-crossing, Wu counterstruck—all war is deception, cashed at campaign scale. Helü's brother Fugai attacked without orders, 'acting as duty demands': display only works when the opponent reads the script, and initiative must pair with it.

C-SW-007E.title_en: Five Victories in Five: the Combo Rhythm of Cheng and Chi
C-SW-007E.description_en: From Boju through Qingfa and Yongshi to Ying, Wu won five battles in succession: the orthodox line pinned Chu's mass while mobile columns struck its seams—the surprise deciding each engagement the moment the regular one locked, cheng and chi transmuting as the front rolled, until Chu was forever answering the last battle and never organizing the next.

C-SW-008E.title_en: Ten Days, Three Hundred Li: Speed at Its Limit
C-SW-008E.description_en: After Boju the Wu army lived off the country, harried the crossings of the Qingfa River, burned its own boats behind it, and covered three hundred li in ten days to enter Ying—Chu's mobilization never completed, its 200,000 frozen unusable by time alone. Yet the deep line proved fragile: Qin relief and Yue raids forced Wu's withdrawal. Speed's gains and speed's debts arrived in the same campaign.

tags_en: Able General Unhands by the Throne
C-SW-009E.title_en: The Uninterfered Commander: Helü and His Generals
C-SW-009E.description_en: Once Sunzi was made general, Helü largely ceased remote-controlling campaigns: Fugai's unauthorized attack at Boju went unpunished, and the six-year harassment rhythm was set in the field—'when the general is able and the sovereign does not interfere, there is victory.' The boundary showed after Ying: as the king indulged in Chu's palace, court will and front-line purpose diverged, and the army withdrew when Qin came to Chu's relief. No interference presumes one will still holds.

C-SW-010E.title_en: Ying Squandered: the Ledger of War Won and Peace Lost
C-SW-010E.description_en: After taking Ying, the Wu command squabbled over Chu's palaces and Wu Zixu whipped the dead king's corpse—'win battles and take cities, yet fail to consolidate the gains, and the outcome is calamity' rehearsed in full: no political settlement for the Chu people, Qin's relief army raised, Yue raided Wu's homeland, and the conquerors abandoned the capital. Sunzi vanishes from the record; the thirteen chapters close on 'the enlightened ruler is prudent, the good general vigilant—the way to secure the state and keep the army whole.' The war that can be won and the war that should be fought are two ledgers.

C-WQ-001E.title_en: High-Potential Selection: An Open Exam with Household Benefits
C-WQ-001E.description_en: A manufacturing group debates referral versus open examination for its critical-equipment engineer track. The wuzu method wins: skills published (loaded maintenance, fault-finding, timed standards); those who pass earn upgraded family health coverage plus child education subsidies — the incentive lands on the household, so training becomes family investment. Within three years the track is the group's crown asset in M&A talks.

C-WQ-002E.title_en: Security Budget Fight: Cameras or Community
C-WQ-002E.description_en: A district doubles its security budget; every proposal buys cameras and fences. A Wu Qi twin-track audit shows half of incidents trace to neighbour conflict and service gaps. Final split: 60% technology, 40% community services. Two years on, incident reduction beats the pure-tech simulation.

C-WQ-003E.title_en: M&A Due Diligence with a Symmetric Checklist
C-WQ-003E.description_en: A deal team collects only bullish signals on a target. The strike/spare checklist is imposed: attackable signals (customer concentration, key departures) and do-not-attack signals (stable cash flow, founder buyback pledge) on one table, each weakness time-boxed. Price pressed inside the window; no close by expiry, deal withdrawn.

C-WQ-004E.description_en: A newly hired sales director meets resistance. Following shared hardship: a published list of surrendered privileges (travel standard aligned with the field, weekly ride-alongs), visible cost paid before targets are demanded — while performance rules stay rigid. In six months voluntary overtime rises and attrition falls: warmth and discipline on one track.

C-WQ-005E.title_en: Phased Morale Management in a Call Centre
C-WQ-005E.description_en: A call centre sees attrition spike each peak season. Rebuilt on 'instruction first' in phases: onboarding exhausts errors in safety (reserve), scheduling prevents stacked pressure (muster), peak hours run standard scripts and signals (battle), rewards paid publicly on the spot (after action). Morale is managed as inventory, not a town-hall speech.

C-WQ-006E.title_en: A Competitive Playbook for the Giant's Entry
C-WQ-006E.description_en: A startup learns a giant will launch a rival product. A situation-response mapping is built: price war (premise: their margin structure) -> bind vertical scenarios; poaching -> pre-signed equity locks for cores; acquisition rumour -> defensive financing. Each template carries premises and expiry conditions, refreshed quarterly.

C-WQ-007E.description_en: Two years of unpaid bonus promises have killed mobilization. On 'if rewards are not trusted, orders will not run': no new promises; historical arrears paid and publicized; one executive breach sanctioned under the same rule as staff, announced to all. Within three months, voluntary uptake of new targets recovers — credibility before content.

C-WQ-008E.title_en: Endowment-to-Role Matching in a Product Team
C-WQ-008E.description_en: A product team rotates staff by performance ranking; everyone is mediocre. The 'short bear the spear' principle re-cuts work into profiles — assault, sustainment, exploration, operations — matching by endowment (deep focus, risk appetite, communication, precision) with specialist training. A year later the assault group ships 40% faster: employ men as instruments.

C-WQ-009E.description_en: A high performer misses promotion twice. The four-account audit (ruler, troops, rival, self) shows: performance full marks, the upward account blank — risks never synced upward, improper skip-level channels. Six months of repair, then a division-general-manager seat. The hardest cell is the self.

C-WQ-010E.description_en: A new CEO drives digital transformation on a single board patron's backing. Wu Qi's lesson is applied: while the patron serves, weld new processes into middle-bench KPIs, showcase beneficiary departments, map post-patron politics in advance. Three years later the patron retires — the processes and coalition stand alone, and the reform does not roll back.
C-WQ-010E.title: Building the Reform's Load-Bearing Structure

Wu Qi's lesson is applied: while the patron serves, weld new processes into middle-bench KPIs, showcase beneficiary departments, map post-patron politics in advance. C-CW-001E.title_en: The Political-Object Audit of a Price War
C-CW-001E.description_en: A retail chain is pushed by capital into a price war for market share. The Clausewitzian audit comes first: write the political object — what share of premium members must the customer base hold after the war — then scale the violence to the object. Each discount round is converted into 'did it move the object or only burn cash?' Two rounds in, they find clearance pricing grows GMV but not the object, and pivot to member depth, de-escalating the price war to local defence.
C-CW-001E.title: The Political-Object Audit of a Price War

C-CW-002E.title_en: Friction Margins in a Core-System Migration
C-CW-002E.description_en: A bank's core-system migration plan promised 'six weeks, zero failures.' Rebuilt with friction as a constant: only phase lines (dual-write, staged cutover, rollback points); resources budgeted at twice the adverse case; engineers empowered to halt within a phase line. On day ten an unforecast data-format mismatch appeared — and never became an incident, because margin and field authority absorbed it. A full-score execution of 'design for error.'
C-CW-002E.title: Friction Margins in a Core-System Migration

C-CW-003E.title_en: Due Diligence on the Rival's Center of Gravity
C-CW-003E.description_en: Two firms bid for the same asset. Bidder B skips the bidding war and first maps A's dependency structure: one client supplies sixty percent of revenue, and core capacity sits in a single plant. B concentrates its pitch on those two hubs with differentiated commitments and wins at a lower overall score — find the rival's center of gravity first, then decide where to spend force.
C-CW-003E.title: Due Diligence on the Rival's Center of Gravity

C-CW-004E.title_en: War-Gaming the Escalation Ladder with a Regulator
C-CW-004E.description_en: A platform battered by new rules hears 'fight everything' from its PR team. The Clausewitzian three beats: compute the logical limit (unrestrained, both sides lose licenses); compute the real constraints (the regulator's toolkit, media windows, rivals' moves); then the board picks the rung — compliance appeal plus partial remediation — with escalation triggers predefined. Six months later the rule is revised and the platform wins its main point at minimum intensity.
C-CW-004E.title: War-Gaming the Escalation Ladder with a Regulator

C-CW-005E.description_en: A new entrant attacks the delivery market at five yuan of subsidy per order. The incumbent refuses to match and instead plots the attacker's culminating point: funding cadence and burn rate say subsidies cannot last past month fourteen. A strong defence — membership plus exclusive restaurant contracts — holds the line; in month fifteen the subsidies taper, and the incumbent counter-attacks the loosened cities with its banked partner resources.
C-CW-005E.title: Waiting Out the Subsidy War

C-CW-006E.title_en: Community as the Lever in a Product Crisis
C-CW-006E.description_en: An open-source software firm faces a closed-source rival going free. Instead of matching marketing spend, it turns to the community: roadmap voting and security-audit bounties open to core contributors — the community becomes a social force money cannot buy, and third-party ecosystems ship adversarial integrations on their own. Six months after the free version launches, the migration rate is under three percent.
C-CW-006E.title: Community as the Lever in a Product Crisis

C-CW-007E.title_en: A Decide-On-Time Protocol When Data Runs Short
C-CW-007E.description_en: A fund's analysts always need 'one more document' before flagging a collapsing position. The Clausewitzian inner question is institutionalized: a decide-on-time protocol — when the data window closes, they must answer 'what must be settled now, and what does delay cost,' with a monthly audit of hit rates on decisions made under incomplete information. In the next crisis the team exits at seventy percent information and misses the full collapse.
C-CW-007E.title: A Decide-On-Time Protocol When Data Runs Short

C-CW-008E.description_en: A tea-brand franchise sprints to two thousand stores. The culminating-point calculation follows: franchisee-return decay, quality-control cost, and brand dilution computed segment by segment along the growth curve mark three thousand stores as the political-military peak; the organizational conversion from expansion to consolidation (supervision, direct supply control) completes before it. Rival chains push to five thousand and break out in closures; culminating-point management preserves the core business.
C-CW-008E.title: Culminating-Point Metrics for Expansion

C-CW-009E.title_en: The Symmetric Ledger in Strategy Reviews
C-CW-009E.description_en: A company's quarterly review had become a praise session. The critical method is installed: state the quarter's theoretical claim first ('paid acquisition builds brand equity'), then keep a symmetric ledger — data where the claim held and where it broke are booked separately, and 'poor execution' is banned as a universal solvent. Three quarters later the theory's scope is explicit: acquisition works for new products, backfires on mature ones, and budgets are re-ranked.
C-CW-009E.title: The Symmetric Ledger in Strategy Reviews

C-CW-010E.title_en: Three Reins on an Information War
C-CW-010E.description_en: A company caught in a PR storm sees its team radicalize and demand 'all-out war.' The board holds three reins: monitor public sentiment and the opponent's escalation moves; lock the response scope and exit conditions in advance; hand operational detail fully to the PR team — the board reviews only object and limits. Ten days later the storm passes naturally, and the firm keeps brand trust at minimal intensity.
C-CW-010E.title: Three Reins on an Information War

C-LH-001E.description_en: A SaaS company challenges the incumbent's core market. Instead of feature-for-feature parity, it drafts the dislocation list first: sixty percent of rival revenue locked in an aging delivery model, its three largest clients renewing in the same month, a single-timezone support team. The challenger spends a year building compatibility layers and migration tools to cut the 'communications,' and opens battle only when the rival's key clients waver — the signing war ends in three months, a settlement rather than a gamble.
C-LH-001E.title: Dislocation Design Before the Showdown

C-LH-002E.description_en: A tool product's single-channel growth stalls and the team wants to 'push harder.' They switch to expansion waves: every push pre-sets culminating metrics (acquisition-cost decay, referral coefficient); when wave one's thrust flags, wave two — new category, new region — passes its flank, and budget piling into the proven corridor is banned. Three alternating waves double annual growth without a single push to collapse.
C-LH-002E.title: Wave Design for Growth

C-LH-003E.title_en: Organizational Revolution Before the AI Tool
C-LH-003E.description_en: A law firm buys the most expensive legal AI and bolts it into existing workflows; nobody uses it. Redone on technology-organization co-evolution: first answer what new division of labor the tool demands — juniors become reviewers rather than retrievers, partners sign a new attestation form, billing structures rewritten. Only after reorganizing does the rollout happen; six months on, usage is ninety percent. The technology never changed — the composition did.
C-LH-003E.title: Organizational Revolution Before the AI Tool

C-LH-004E.title_en: The Limited Aim in a Patent War
C-LH-004E.description_en: A hardware firm is sued on patents, and management wants to 'litigate the rival into bankruptcy.' The limited-war reset: the aim's ceiling is written as 'cross-license plus rival exit from our two core markets,' means restricted to a specific patent pool and compliance filings, escalation into mutual suits refused. Fourteen months later the settlement lands — the cost of total litigation and ecosystem revenge both avoided, and the peace is better than before the war.
C-LH-004E.title: The Limited Aim in a Patent War

C-LH-005E.title_en: The Resistance Quotient for Market Entry
C-LH-005E.description_en: A beverage company expands; the board all favors 'the biggest tier-one cities.' Computing the resistance quotient — competitive density over speed of entry — for every candidate: tier-one density is extreme and approvals slow (highest quotient), while prefecture cities at two provinces' seam have near-zero density and fast logistics (lowest). Resources concentrate on the seam cluster as the decision point; regional density leadership in a year, then leverage to re-enter tier one from a base.
C-LH-005E.title: The Resistance Quotient for Market Entry

C-LH-006E.title_en: Decay-Curve Audit of the Viral Launch
C-LH-006E.description_en: A consumer brand bets on 'one mega-marketing event to ignite everything.' The decay-curve audit: four weeks post-event the rival copies the spend, twelve weeks the platform algorithm changes — first-strike dividend at zero and repeat-purchase structure nonexistent. The plan is refused in favor of a cumulative strategy (membership system plus supply-chain moat) pushed in eighteen waves. Two years later the rival does copy the event — and cannot dent the retention structure.
C-LH-006E.title: Decay-Curve Audit of the Viral Launch

C-LH-007E.description_en: A fund studies the sell-side consensus that 'consumer downtrading is a decade-long trend.' The Liddell Hart method forces counterexample collection: three interviews with the failed (chain founders who closed), two with the marginal (downmarket supply-chain operators), one cross-domain (a resale-platform operator). The counterexamples show downtrading and up-grading coexist; the consensus's domain is rewritten to 'specific categories.' The portfolio avoids a systemic mismatch.
C-LH-007E.title: Counterexample Interviews Against Consensus

C-LH-008E.title_en: Elite Squads at the Lever Points
C-LH-008E.description_en: A mid-sized industrial-software vendor, dwarfed by giants, abandons the full product-line race and designs backward from lever points: three hub scenarios — a data interface for a flagship industry, a seat on the standards committee, a joint lab with one anchor customer — each staffed with an elite squad carrying a pre-written exit (sellable, mergable). Three years later these hubs deliver half the industry's inbound traffic, and alliance partners treat the firm as the de-facto standard partner.
C-LH-008E.title: Elite Squads at the Lever Points

C-LH-009E.title_en: Premise-Year Audit of the Winning Business
C-LH-009E.description_en: A retailer's most profitable business is a franchise system built ten years ago. A semiannual premise-year audit asks which technology cycle its three success assumptions (information asymmetry, logistics cost, consumption radius) were born in — two are outdated. Review and new experiments (a gray-launch of direct-operated cloud warehouses) start at once; three years later, when the old system declines naturally, the new one has taken over — avoiding the collapse of 'preparing for the last war.'
C-LH-009E.title: Premise-Year Audit of the Winning Business

C-LH-010E.title_en: The Double-Optimum Test for a Growth Hack
C-LH-010E.description_en: A growth team proposes 'misusing a system pop-up to misdirect complaints at a rival,' with attractive short-term projections. The double-optimum test: the moral failure point (manipulating users) and the strategic failure point (platform bans, talent revulsion) coincide at one spot — the plan is refused. The team pivots to recommendation improvements that genuinely benefit users; three months later retention rises, with no ruins left to tidy.
C-LH-010E.title: The Double-Optimum Test for a Growth Hack

C-YC-001E.description_en: A nonprofit ran county digital-literacy classes designed as 'teaching elders to use smartphones.' Two weeks of village residency revealed elders already selling mountain goods via short video, self-taught. The project pivoted to 'turn your selling account into a real business' — bookkeeping, sourcing, service scripts. Attendance rose from thirty to ninety percent: the elders never changed; the project's subject-credo did.
C-YC-001E.title: Revaluing the Served Community

C-YC-002E.title_en: The Four-Diagnosis Audit of a Region
C-YC-002E.description_en: A retail chain's East-China region kept sliding and headquarters wanted to replace its head. The four diagnoses: 40% failing new-product quizzes (ignorance), commission rules frozen two years while rivals raised pay (poverty), chronic understaffing (weakness), cross-store buck-passing (selfishness). Four prescriptions ran in parallel; two quarters later performance recovered and the personnel change was scrapped — the disease was in the diagnosis, not the person.
C-YC-002E.title: The Four-Diagnosis Audit of a Region

C-YC-003E.description_en: A vocational college took a generic e-commerce course to county markets. The fourfold match rebuilt it: 'can't choose products' got a hands-on sourcing line; 'no capital' got micro-credit plus group purchasing; 'burned out livestreaming' got health-and-scheduling guidance; 'alone' got a local sellers' mutual-aid society. Four lines enrolled in parallel; three-month survival of graduates far outpaced the generic course.
C-YC-003E.title: Prescription-Matched County Courses

C-YC-004E.title_en: Back-Deriving the Course from the Pain List
C-YC-004E.description_en: A SaaS firm's customer-success team was to learn data analytics, starting from SQL syntax. Need-as-curriculum redid it: the week's real problems were surveyed — 'why is the renewal rate falling?' ranked first. Lesson one built that renewal-decomposition table directly, with SQL as a later footnote. Trainees used it in customer meetings that same week; completion rose from 55% to 92%.
C-YC-004E.title: Back-Deriving the Course from the Pain List

C-YC-005E.title_en: The Residency Order for the Product Team
C-YC-005E.description_en: An agri-input e-commerce firm 'studied farmers remotely.' A doctors-to-the-villages rule was set: product, operations, and supply-chain leads each embedded in a village for a month, sharing meals and farming seasons, with proposals required to quote farmers' words and participation. A month later the flagship 'smart fertilizer-mixing' feature was cut (a farmer's words: 'I trust Old Zhou in town') in favor of onboarding technicians like Zhou — GMV and retention both rose.
C-YC-005E.title: The Residency Order for the Product Team

C-YC-006E.description_en: A factory's safety training attendance was chronically low. Three-approach redesign: school approach — mandatory onboarding module with assessment; social approach — weekly incident postmortems on shop-floor boards and two-minute pre-shift talks; family approach — a 'home safety card' mailed to families, employees asked to explain it at home and sign. All three channels owned one metric, hazard-reporting rate; in half a year it quadrupled and accidents hit a record low.
C-YC-006E.title: Three Channels for Safety Training

C-YC-007E.title_en: A Career Track for Village Teachers
C-YC-007E.description_en: A nonprofit lost over half its young teachers within two years. Professionalized vocation redesign: selection kept 'creed plus village probation'; pay published as 'below city but enough to settle a household,' with housing; an in-house teaching-research ladder with public lectures; international education conferences offered speaking seats. Two years on, attrition fell to ten percent, and candidates now compete for county research-lead posts — the mission became a track.
C-YC-007E.title: A Career Track for Village Teachers

C-YC-008E.title_en: Handover Clauses for the Innovation Pilot
C-YC-008E.description_en: A bank's digital-branch pilot had run three years as a permanent 'special zone.' The experiment-institution split fixed it: handover clauses written first — success criteria (self-service rate, cost), the taking-over department, budget lines, exit date; the innovation group shipped 'experience packages' (processes, staffing, cost tables) and operations absorbed them into routine while the pilot was dissolved. Twenty branches converted in half a year; the group moved to its next experiment.
C-YC-008E.title: Handover Clauses for the Innovation Pilot

C-YC-009E.title_en: Clean Water the Poorest County Can Pay For
C-YC-009E.description_en: A water project originally designed 'one standardized station per village' priced beyond most counties' upkeep. Low-cost-replicability redesign took the poorest county's annual O&M budget as the hard cap: one water steward per village trained in three days, locally made filter drums, rapid-test cards — the minimum viable dose; manuals localized, graduated stewards teaching neighboring villages. Three years later a hundred villages ran with zero head-office subsidy.
C-YC-009E.title: Clean Water the Poorest County Can Pay For

C-YC-010E.title_en: The Failure Column in the Annual Report
C-YC-010E.description_en: An education foundation's annual report carried only success stories until funders began doubting the data. The Ding Xian loop reform: acceptance cards signed before every project, an 'unmet-targets column' in the report with causes and corrective constraints, public self-critique converted into next-year's hard clauses. Seven unmet projects were published in year one — and two funders increased their grants: credibility itself became a fundraising asset.
C-YC-010E.title: The Failure Column in the Annual Report

C-TXZ-001E.description_en: A manufacturer's off-site training left learners 'moved in class, inert on the floor.' The new training lead audited the shop's real life: the learning already happening was veterans' firefighting and oral craft. Budget shifted to a 'field-project system' — each crew takes one real improvement project per quarter, with classes only when the project jams. A year on, 37 improvements shipped and the training room became an exhibition hall.

C-TXZ-002E.title_en: The Corporate University With No Campus
C-TXZ-002E.description_en: A retail chain's 'corporate university' sat empty — the stores were too far. The team made every store a branch: 'today's question' by the till, morning briefings built on real complaints, store managers as lecturers. Six months later learning touchpoints covered the whole chain and the 'university' shrank to one operations cell — maintaining a network, not a property.

C-TXZ-003E.title_en: An Internship Built on One Real Delivery
C-TXZ-003E.description_en: A software firm found interns 'theoretical until broken by reality.' They switched to unity of teaching-learning-doing: each intern takes one real small delivery on day one (fix and ship a real minor defect), the mentor teaches on demand from 'what finishing it requires,' with a forecast before and a retrospective after. Independent-delivery rates across three cohorts rose from 20% to 90%.

C-TXZ-004E.description_en: An NGO training rural teachers in digital tools faced thin staffing. The rule became 'transmit as you know': graduation required teaching two colleagues back home and leaving a teaching record in the group. Three cohorts later, coverage rolled from 40 to over 300 — same budget, transmission switched from linear to compound.

C-TXZ-005E.description_en: A PM insisted on 'understanding users fully before acting' and shipped nothing for six months. The director's new rule: tag every claim 'first-hand or heard' — judgments with no user contact are heard-knowledge, low credence; one real visit per month as the 'first-hand quota.' Three months on, paper debates thinned and small iterations driven by real counterexamples multiplied.

C-TXZ-006E.title_en: A Six-Liberation Audit of the Team
C-TXZ-006E.description_en: A company proclaimed innovation with no innovators. Management self-audited on the six liberations: thinking (occupied by KPIs), doing (no experiment rights), seeing (never meets customers), speaking (proposals unanswered), space (never leaves the desk), time (meeting-stuffed). They unbound as a set: a monthly customer day, 20% experiment time, answers to proposals within seven days. Funded proposals rose fivefold in a quarter.

C-TXZ-007E.title_en: The Trust Wall in a Training Business
C-TXZ-007E.description_en: An academy paid lecturers on renewal commissions and sales talk crept into the courseware. The principal re-established trust rules: courseware review walled off from sales metrics, lecturers barred from selling add-ons, pricing published. Renewals dipped 10% for a season; a year later word-of-mouth referral was the top channel — trust compounds.

C-TXZ-008E.description_en: A factory promoted by credentials and tenure while veterans' field fixes scattered across workshops. The new system opened a 'small creation registry': any post's improvement — a saved step, a saved watt, a saved minute — is registered under its author's name and enters review. Year one logged 412 entries, 11 spread plant-wide: the criterion moved from 'rank and years' to 'what did you solve.'

C-TXZ-009E.title_en: Run One Crew First, Scale Later
C-TXZ-009E.description_en: A plant's new scheduling scheme had been revised eight times at HQ and still hadn't landed. The new director reversed course: pilot in the hardest crew at 'zero budget,' books and problems fully open, one quarter of running, then a two-page memo of transferable elements. HQ stopped asking 'is it feasible' and asked 'how many crews next quarter.'

C-TXZ-010E.description_en: A company hung 'democratic management' banners and nothing changed. Management turned democracy into daily practice: monthly budgets open to all, proposals answered on a deadline, rotating chairs for meetings. Six months on, proposals were mostly small process fixes — and every one landed. For the first time, employees felt the company belonged to 'all of us.'

C-CYP-001E.description_en: A research institute's new director found the lab used as a 'title-stamping station' for promotions. Before touching any structure he issued an ontological address: 'This institute produces knowledge, not titles,' paired with a three-question audit (what did you come to do? what will you deliver? what are you doing now?). Within six months the credential-collectors drifted away on their own, and genuine researchers received full resources for the first time.

C-CYP-002E.description_en: A company's executives deadlocked over a single architecture route. The CTO applied 'inclusiveness': two routes with equal budgets and identical assessment, quarterly public data comparison, and a referee who audits only data integrity — never judges the route. Two quarters later the market's data picked the winner, and the losing team's core members folded their experience into the winner's track — competition achieved what personnel orders could not.

C-CYP-003E.title_en: Restoring the Missing Aims in a KPI System
C-CYP-003E.description_en: An education company's reviews tracked revenue alone; support quality kept decaying. A five-fold audit found 'ethics and aesthetics' at zero institutional supply. Both were written in as rigid metrics — an aesthetic content review board plus a refunds-rate moral red line — with non-raidable weights. Two quarters later refunds fell 40% and revenue rose on reputation: plural aims are guardrails, not burdens.

C-CYP-004E.title_en: Meeting Emotional Needs with Public Supply
C-CYP-004E.description_en: In a large community, radicalizing groups grew active. The operator diagnosed a 'belonging-supply shortage' and, instead of policing speech, launched free choirs, reading circles, and markets — emotional shelter as routine public provision. A year on, shares of extremist content fell 70%: the demand for feeling was caught by a better device.

C-CYP-005E.title_en: A Technical Council Takes the Architecture Keys
C-CYP-005E.description_en: Architecture at a platform company was long decided by one CTO; rework rates stayed high. A new charter created a technical council of fifteen engineer-elected members; architecture decisions pass the council by vote, with the executive line retaining a bounded execution veto. Within a year major rework halved and attrition fell in step — power follows expertise, and accountability gains a direction.

C-CYP-006E.title_en: An Offer Letter Without a Degree Gate
C-CYP-006E.description_en: A security lab couldn't fill a cryptography seat; doctoral candidates all declined. The lead switched to the 'talent principle': a public call for verifiable decryption records and open-source work, ending with the hire of a self-taught analyst — an exam-based bachelor's degree, but a GitHub of consistently strong crypto libraries. Two years later he anchors the team: the currency of evaluation changed from diploma to performance.

C-CYP-007E.description_en: A procurement-heavy company could not stop vendor kickbacks. The Virtue-Society answer: tiered pledges — everyone signs the base tier (no cash or gift cards); procurement and engineering may opt into the advanced tier (relative-recusal, interest disclosure); rosters and violations searchable by all; the founding team signed first. Two years on, procurement costs fell 9% — the reputation mechanism began to run.

C-CYP-008E.description_en: A manufacturer wanted data analysts but could not fund full-time study. HR designed 'work for tuition': three days a week on data-related production tasks (credited against fees), two days in class, with a directed transfer on completion; the company centrally handled scheduling and mentor matching. Three cohorts graduated 42, with 31 transferred — at a third the cost of external hiring.

C-CYP-009E.title_en: A Separate Institute for Long-Horizon Research
C-CYP-009E.description_en: Battery basics research at a carmaker was perpetually squeezed by product units. Management chartered a separate institute: its own budget, researcher ranks parallel to management's, dual-track publication (papers and patents), and mandatory international conferences. Two years without direct output; in year five its solid-state electrolyte work fed the product line — new functions need new establishments, not 'side duties' in old departments.

C-CYP-010E.description_en: A data company's VP of engineering found management tolerating doctored user metrics. Six months earlier she had written 'data integrity' into her published principles and completed handover institutions (a review council plus succession rules). Now she resigned per her stated terms with a signed statement. The stock wobbled short-term, but the board ordered an independent inquiry and hired a compliance chief — a prepared exit is not abandonment; it is a handover with limits attached.

C-DY-001E.description_en: Half of a secondary school's timetable was suspended drills 'for the exam three years away,' leaving students drained in class and hollow after. The dean began with a preparationist-debt audit: every period that could not answer 'what does this mean for a sixteen-year-old right now' was rebuilt — English became running a campus podcast, math anchored to a real finance project. Two years on, exam results rose rather than fell: experience had gained continuity, and test scores were a by-product.

C-DY-002E.title_en: A Quarterly Review Starting from 'What Broke'
C-DY-002E.description_en: A software firm's quarterly reviews had become award ceremonies. The new procedure starts from the theory of inquiry: no summaries beforehand — first freeze the raw record of 'what actually broke' (tickets, alerts, customer quotes), then run controlled inquiry, each conclusion carrying evidence and a boundary of failure. Two seasons later, the review's product changed from 'lessons-learned slides' into a decision-tool library with failure conditions attached.

C-DY-003E.title_en: The Campus Parcel Desk as Social Studies
C-DY-003E.description_en: A primary school's 'social studies' had shrunk to a textbook. The school handed a real parcel desk to fifth graders: pricing, scheduling, lost-item compensation, open accounts. The 'realness' criterion ran every link — failure carried real cost, success had real beneficiaries. Within a term, literacy, arithmetic, and dispute negotiation grew inside the business's needs, and parents moved from skeptics to volunteers.

C-DY-004E.title_en: One Sentence: Writing the Feeling as a Problem
C-DY-004E.description_en: A design firm's review meetings talked past one another. New rule: before any proposal is discussed, the team co-writes a one-sentence statement of 'what the real problem is,' and no solutions enter until everyone can restate it identically; major decisions run at least two hypotheses to testable consequences. Three months later meetings ran at half length — the highest value was added at problematization.

C-DY-005E.title_en: Onboarding Grown from a Real Delivery
C-DY-005E.description_en: A company's onboarding was three weeks of generic courseware, forgotten at certification. They switched to purposeful occupation: each newcomer takes one real small delivery in week one (fix a real defect and ship it), with knowledge taught at the point of need — 'what finishing it requires' — and outputs facing real users. Independent-delivery rates across three cohorts rose from 30% to 85%.

C-DY-006E.description_en: A firm's training scored high on satisfaction and low on behavior change. The L&D team scored every course on continuity x interaction: interfaces with learners' past and future experience, and two-way engagement with the real environment. Double-low courses were rebuilt — cases replaced by the learner's own real projects, plus a three-month on-the-job application window. Behavior-change rates doubled the next year.

C-DY-007E.description_en: A company rolled out 'democratic management' — voting complete, participation thin. Management switched to the communicative criterion: whose voice never appears in meeting minutes? How many layers does information climb? They built the communication infrastructure first — pre-published proposals, cross-level co-research groups, decision feedback loops — and restored voting after half a year: participation rose from 10% to 70%.

C-DY-008E.description_en: A training company's KPIs all descended from headquarters; instructors and learners were consumables. The new head ran an aim-source audit: for each metric — who set it, for whose interest, what do learners experience now? Metrics failing the three questions were abolished; 'competency directions' were rewritten into concrete aims the learners themselves proposed, revisable each term. Within a year, renewals and reputation both rose.

C-DY-009E.title_en: Adding the Industry Course to the Skills Course
C-DY-009E.description_en: A vocational school's short programs placed graduates well, yet three-year job-transition rates were dismal — the narrower the skill, the faster the obsolescence. The school audited the 'about occupation' ratio: every skills course now carries industry history, economic structure, and transition paths, with skill maps and pay data open school-wide. Starting salaries held, but five-year cross-role and promotion rates doubled — education had given them the capacity to choose again.

C-DY-010E.title_en: A Public Reckoning of One's Own Method
C-DY-010E.description_en: A consultancy's 'agile transformation' engagements kept collapsing — clients had turned agile into a daily-standup performance. The partners did not disown the clients; they published a public reckoning: diagnosing the abuse forms item by item with agile's core concepts, separating 'execution to abandon' from 'core to keep,' with a revised implementation checklist. The report became a cited industry text, and the firm's standing rose.

C-MV-001E.description_en: Half of a secondary school's timetable was suspended drills 'for the exam three years away,' leaving students drained in class and hollow after. The dean began with a preparationist-debt audit: every period that could not answer 'what does this mean for a sixteen-year-old right now' was rebuilt — English became running a campus podcast, math anchored to a real finance project. Two years on, exam results rose rather than fell: experience had gained continuity, and test scores were a by-product.

C-MV-002E.title_en: A Quarterly Report Evolves into 'Three-Source Reconciliation'
C-MV-002E.description_en: A company's quarterly results long rested on a single dashboard — until one season's data diverged so badly from the books that the error was caught externally. The CFO introduced 'compass × star-chart × landmark' triangulation: estimated figures, financial accounts and actual customer payments reconciled line by line, with any gap over 2% freezing publication until the model was fixed. The next divergence was caught three days before release, averting a credibility incident with external numbers.

C-MV-003E.title_en: A Three-Step Response After a Rival Crosses the Line
C-MV-003E.description_en: A rival suddenly poached an entire team and spread misleading comparisons. Management resisted the urge to 'fight everywhere,' working a three-step ladder: private channels for retraction first, then a public data clarification, and only after continued crossing did they strike back — precisely, in a single market. Six months later the industry consensus was 'principled but willing to hit,' and small clashes actually declined.

C-MV-004E.title_en: Shelving the Overseas Warehouse by Portfolio
C-MV-004E.description_en: A go-abroad team wanted to bet one country's market on a single hit product. The supply-chain lead rebuilt the plan on the treasure-shelf method: per-port demand research first, then 60% flagship + 30% staples + 10% probes, with barter and a third currency as fallback settlement if the exchange rate broke. When the flagship flopped in the first peak season, the staples' cash flow carried the warehouse rent — the team survived into season two.

C-MV-005E.description_en: Overseas teams returned to only verbal debriefs, and the next cohort paid the same tuition. The company created a 'record-keeper' post: every deployment produces a structured report (channels / prices / policies / pitfalls) filed into a shared base, and every departure reads the last debrief first. Three cycles on, first-quarter mistakes by newcomers dropped by seventy percent — knowledge sedimented with the routes.

C-MV-006E.description_en: A project team spanning five time zones ran 'everyone live at all times' into severe burnout. They switched to protocol coordination: a shared rhythm calendar, one fixed daily re-sync point, pre-shared contingency parameters if contact was lost 24 hours, frontline autonomy on routine matters with mandatory escalation for system-level calls. Three months later meeting time halved and delivery rhythm grew steadier.

C-MV-007E.description_en: A legacy company appointed an outside expert with no factional base to lead transformation — reporting straight to the chair, fluent in two industries. Some called it 'immature'; the chair valued exactly his single-line loyalty and cross-boundary interface. Transformation landed in two years — and the board hedged in parallel: the methodology was written into institutional documents, tied to no single person.

C-MV-008E.description_en: A platform declined to acquire its small service partners, instead designing tiered certification: gold / silver / bronze partners earn traffic, training and co-selling rights by depth, with rankings and investiture ceremonies made public. Partners invested in themselves to climb; the platform kept order with zero onsite management. Two years on, top-partner renewal hit 95%.

C-MV-009E.title_en: Writing the Buying Season into the Product Calendar
C-MV-009E.description_en: A company long shipped by internal schedule, repeatedly landing at the tail of the industry's buying season. Strategy rewrote the plan as a rhythm calendar: customer budget seasons, trade shows and policy windows went directly into the release plan, and waiting periods were booked as planned cost, not failure. Release hit-rate rose from 40% to 85%, and the team stopped apologizing for 'being slow.'

C-MV-010E.title_en: The Evidence of Silence: An Archive-Discontinuity Audit
C-MV-010E.description_en: Post-acquisition, the buyer found that three years of 'should-exist' meeting minutes and contract annexes were massively missing. The audit refused to rest on testimony, running four steps: list the records that should exist, classify the mode of absence (lost / destroyed / never produced), build physical time anchors from bank flows and mail-server logs, and ask 'who needs this version of the story.' Conclusion: the gaps clustered in two tenures, pointing to deliberate purge rather than carelessness.

C-AE-001E.title_en: Writing Uncertainty into the Financing Terms
C-AE-001E.description_en: A biotech team pitching investors faced a pipeline of unknowable outcome. Instead of overselling, they wrote milestones, failure tolerance and tiered profit-sharing into the term sheet: funders paid by stage, the team kept execution control, and success was shared by outcome. When the lead pipeline failed in Series B, the clauses allowed contraction and retry — two years later the second pipeline won approval, and no one accused anyone of 'overpromising at the start.'

C-AE-002E.title_en: Heterogeneous Redundancy in a Cross-Border Team
C-AE-002E.description_en: A company going abroad had staked its entire supply-chain competence on one nationality of staff; a political shock paralyzed everything. After restructuring, every critical function was covered by people of two or more different backgrounds, with language and compliance talent hired backwards from the target market. In the next regional turmoil, a single departure caused no capability gap.

C-AE-003E.title_en: Segmented Elimination for a Technical Route
C-AE-003E.description_en: An R&D team argued for six months between two technical routes. The chief engineer switched to segmented elimination: slice the big question into auditable small experiments, each with a fixed 'pass / no pass' verdict filed in the archive, negative results included and reusable. Three quarters later the elimination chain converged on its own, and the route was settled by data, not decibels.

C-AE-004E.title_en: Start Rationing at the First Squeeze
C-AE-004E.description_en: When the first sign of delayed receivables appeared, a company froze non-core spend and cut internal consumption — not waiting for empty coffers. Outward communication kept direction and confidence; inward discipline ran on worst-case assumptions. Three months later receivables recovered, and the company outlived two rivals that had been 'optimistic to death.'

C-AE-005E.title_en: Red Lines on a Fulcrum Alliance
C-AE-005E.description_en: A platform allied with a regional champion who demanded help 'crushing a competitor.' The platform set red lines: co-branding and joint ceremony yes; the core team and main resources never mortgaged. When the ally fell into its own price war, the platform — having never bet its core — walked away untouched, and the renewal ran deeper.

C-AE-006E.title_en: An Independent Recorder on Major Projects
C-AE-006E.description_en: After a two-year engineering project shipped, the retro found nobody could say 'why we decided that back then.' From then on every major project carried an independent recorder post (outside the execution chain), with decision and narrative logs archived on dual tracks, failures and casualties included. At acceptance, the archive was delivered as an asset equal to the result.

C-AE-007E.title_en: The Successor's First Week of Contraction
C-AE-007E.description_en: When the founder left abruptly, the successor spent week one not on expansion but on goal-contraction and asset inventory: cut the unfeedable lines, merge people into units that could live, settle the cut units with dignity. The company shrank to sixty percent — and within two years led its remaining market outright.

C-AE-008E.description_en: A product team deadlocked on three open questions. They merged all three into one executable controlled pilot, criteria fixed first, data to speak. When the pilot ended, three debates closed at once and the verdicts went straight into the spec — never again re-litigated with each change of staff.

C-AE-009E.title_en: Positioning in the Regulatory Window, and Exiting
C-AE-009E.description_en: A fintech positioned a new business in the gap before detailed regulation landed — while pre-forecasting the window's closing date and designing its exit (compliance or sale). When the window closed as forecast, two competitors were fined; the company, having monetized in advance, walked away whole.

C-AE-010E.title_en: Adding a Cost Page to Every Success Retro
C-AE-010E.description_en: At a star project's celebration, the CEO required the retro to carry a 'cost page': full-scope personnel loss, capital tied up and opportunity cost presented beside the gain; leadership errors and external risks listed separately; omitted marginal contributors credited on the spot. From then on every success case carried its own cost page — copiers read the costs before learning the moves.

C-AE-011E.description_en: A company adopts a new demand-forecasting system but does not replace the old process outright: both run in parallel for a full business cycle, the new system predicting daily while the old method cross-checks, any divergence triggering manual audit. Three months later the firm holds a complete error archive across extreme and routine conditions — the system enters production on data, not vendor promises.

C-AE-012E.title_en: When a Protocol Stalls, Let the Leaders Use It
C-AE-012E.description_en: A factory rolls out new safety procedures; frontline workers resist. Instead of more persuasion, managers have foremen visibly comply and wear the new gear first; within two weeks adoption passes half. The manager's summary: 'Workers do not believe manuals; they believe whoever they see using them.'

C-AE-013E.title_en: Turn Your Research Unknowns into a Survey Queue
C-AE-013E.description_en: A consulting team takes on an unfamiliar industry study and, instead of open-ended 'getting to know the field', catalogues unknowns into a survey checklist — competitive structure, cost base, regulatory boundary each with closure criteria. Each completed segment is marked 'charted to here + open questions'; six weeks later the verifiable coverage map becomes the client's decision base for years.

C-AE-014E.title_en: End a Debate with One Systematic Sweep
C-AE-014E.description_en: A firm argues endlessly whether a customer segment is worth serving. The data team stops collecting supporting evidence and instead traverses every predicted use case, archiving negative results too: most scenarios lose money, a few high-value scenarios are clearly identifiable. The debate ends; resources reshuffle at once.

C-AE-015E.title_en: Put Experts on the Team, Not the Letterhead
C-AE-015E.description_en: A manufacturer rebuilding a production line does not hire consultants for monthly reviews; it embeds two process experts into the line team at equal risk, with outputs (parameter libraries, fault archives) structurally archived at project milestones. When the rebuild ends, the firm owns both a line and a reusable process knowledge base.

C-AE-016E.description_en: A multinational entering a new market adds, beyond the commercial team, an explicit local advisor: translating local rules and networks inward, explaining the company outward, with coverage radius and failure plan written into the terms. At the first policy shock the company repositions two weeks early — thanks to this 'living chart'.

C-AE-017E.title_en: High-Intensity Sprints Need a Recovery Rhythm
C-AE-017E.description_en: A team sprints nonstop for three months; morale and quality collapse together. The new lead imposes rhythm: every four weeks a checkpoint clearing provisions (tools, budget), health (checkups, leave), and morale (retro) checklists, recovery co-scheduled with delivery. Output holds, attrition halves.

C-AE-018E.title_en: Manage the Identity Others Read You As
C-AE-018E.description_en: A newly arrived executive finds the local team reads him as 'HQ's executioner' — every action maliciously framed. He does not argue; he publicly resets the symbol (listening rounds, dropping retroactive blame), repositioning before the label hardens, and reform resistance drops sharply.

C-AE-019E.title_en: Put 'Two Ships' Under Your Critical System
C-AE-019E.description_en: A payments company suffered a full-day outage from a single point of failure. Rebuilt on the 'two-ship' principle: two independent implementations run in parallel, outputs cross-checked, either taking over instantly. The structure doubles cost — and lets the company sign minute-level recovery SLAs.

C-AE-020E.title_en: Design Archive Delivery That Needs No Survivors
C-AE-020E.description_en: A company mandates: any major incident's core fact package must reach decision-makers within 24 hours via two independent routes (internal flash + external counsel channel), dependent on no particular person. An incident strikes while executives are all traveling; the archive arrives on schedule — decisions begin before the team is even reachable.

C-MT-001E.title_en: Make 'Seen With My Own Eyes' an Iron Rule
C-MT-001E.description_en: A consulting firm's reports kept being challenged on data provenance. The new partner set one rule: every key figure tagged in three tiers — personally verified / reported / inferred — with hearsay carrying source and a pending-verification flag. Two project cycles later, first-pass acceptance in client due diligence rose from 60% to 95%.

C-MT-002E.description_en: A pharma firm's key experiment ran once and entered the submission, drawing regulator questions on reproducibility. Quality moved to a 'conclusion revisit' rule: critical conclusions must be reproduced by a different person via a second independent route, deviations logged and corrected. The next submission passed with zero defects.

C-MT-003E.title_en: Walk the Real Chain to Its Source
C-MT-003E.description_en: A food company faced opaque-supply accusations that press releases and supplier self-certification could not fix. It walked upstream instead: from finished batches back through farming, feed, and breeding, each segment verified on site and photographed. Three months later it published a full-chain provenance map that became an industry reference for crisis response.

C-MT-004E.title_en: Turn Scattered Cases Into One Sample Series
C-MT-004E.description_en: A retailer fought store problems store by store. Operations locked onto one type — anomalous revenue-per-square-meter — and sampled thirty stores across regions under one framework, building a mechanistic explanation chain: not thirty problems, but one problem in thirty environments. Remediation cost halved.

C-MT-005E.title_en: Send Light Teams Where Others Cannot Go
C-MT-005E.description_en: A research boutique could not match big firms' coverage, so it refocused: a three-person squad plus a local collaboration network, working only county markets big teams cannot enter, ceremonial overhead compressed to the limit, mobility traded for reach.
