Modern drill: Version releases: full regression before release, release notes written, known issues registered—the sealing triptych in its standard software form

C-IBS-001E.title: Ibsen's 'Retrospective-Anatomy Method' applied today
C-IBS-001E.description:
The Ghosts inquest (1881): from an orphanage registration, a thirty-year-old marriage fraud is dug out through one letter and one disease—zero 'events,' all retrospection, the textbook of memory-tragedy
Modern drill: Accident investigation and audit: not 'what next' but 'how was the mine laid'—trace present state back through decision history (ledgers, emails, minutes); 'the past never passed' as the report's first principle

C-IBS-002E.title: Ibsen's 'Subtext-Engineering Method' applied today
C-IBS-002E.description:
Hedda's glass and pistol (1890): all of Hedda Gabler's desire and destruction ride on whether the glass is filled and the pistol handed over—the manifest layer is hospitality, the latent layer is assisted suicide
Modern drill: Negotiation and sales: move real demands off the spoken record into concession order and timing—the quotation lists the price, the pause holds the floor; train teams to read the other side's latent layer

C-IBS-003E.title: Ibsen's 'Life-Lie-Pathology Method' applied today
C-IBS-003E.description:
The Wild Duck's double clinic (1884): Gregers (the truth-fanatic who ruins a girl for 'purity') and the Ekdal household (lie-sustainers) in one waiting room—Ibsen offers no good man to side with
Modern drill: Psychotherapy practice: therapeutic non-disclosure and disclosure timing—the therapist seeks not their own innocence; capacity is the only basis of dosage

C-IBS-004E.title: Ibsen's 'Majority-as-Error Method' applied today
C-IBS-004E.description:
The spa hearing (1882): the doctor's bacterial report against the town's interest representatives with a vote—Ibsen lets 'procedurally correct' wrongly kill the facts, forcing the audience to triage propositions
Modern drill: Science communication: proposition triage on climate and vaccines—'is it warming' takes no vote, 'who pays for mitigation' does; the communicator triages first

C-IBS-005E.title: Ibsen's 'Symbolic-Prop Method' applied today
C-IBS-005E.description:
The duck's garret box (1884): a shot duck that dives = the family = Hedvig = the life-lie, fourfold and never explained—the first 'key prop' of modern drama
Modern drill: Brand and product: compress brand value into an object or interaction already useful in the 'plot'—Apple's unboxing, MUJI's packaging, Tesla's door ceremony; value parasitizing function

C-IBS-006E.title: Ibsen's 'Drawing-Room-Section Method' applied today
C-IBS-006E.description:
A Doll's House's Christmas (1879): one household debt case as a holographic section of women's property rights, marriage law, and the credit system—a decade of parliamentary debate completed under one Christmas tree
Modern drill: Organizational diagnosis: enter a company not via the annual report but via one department's weekly meeting—seating, interruptions, who pours the water; the real power map lives in the meeting, not the org chart

C-IBS-007E.title: Ibsen's 'Departure-Ending Method' applied today
C-IBS-007E.description:
The Doll's House door (1879): one slam as manifesto of modern individualism and unfinished social engineering—the German theatres' imposed gentler ending Ibsen himself damned as 'a barbaric outrage'
Modern drill: Product and strategy decisions: an explicit parked-decisions list for structural questions, published—declaring 'not this quarter' preserves trust better than pretending a solution

C-IBS-008E.title: Ibsen's 'Ideal-Dissection Method' applied today
C-IBS-008E.description:
Brand's 'all or nothing' (1866): refusing, amid plague, to keep back a third of the medicine—the purity of the ideal billing mother, wife, and son with compound interest of 'will'
Modern drill: Tech ethics: output-audits for enshrined words—'innovation,' 'connecting the world,' 'free'—an audit table of ideal-words for the attention economy

C-IBS-009E.title: Ibsen's 'Self-Judgment-Writing Method' applied today
C-IBS-009E.description:
Solness as Ibsen's case file (1892): the young worshipper Hilda, the morbid fear of 'the young,' the vanity of the tower-top wreath—every charge preserved in dramatic evidence
Modern drill: Technical writing and post-mortems: the 'include your own bugs' clause—the author of the incident report must appear in the causes list

C-IBS-010E.title: Ibsen's 'Foreign-Lens-Diagnosis Method' applied today
C-IBS-010E.description:
The eight problem plays' offshore production (1877-91): holographic Norwegian parlors written from Germany and Italy—locally pathologizing reports manufactured offshore
Modern drill: Organizational diagnosis: institutionalizing the exit interview—'understood the company only after leaving' as a formal information source; expatriate-repatriate cycle design

C-NOB-001E.title: Nobel's 'Hazard-Domestication Method' applied today
C-NOB-001E.description:
The blasting cap (1863): 'a small controlled blast exciting a large detonation'—the timing point solved alone, giving high explosives their first switch
Modern drill: Nuclear and chemical safety: control rods, redundant seals, emergency cooling—the standard modern implementation of 'valve by valve, keep one in reserve'; chapter one of every safety report is the lost-control inventory

C-NOB-002E.title: Nobel's 'Obituary-Mirror Method' applied today
C-NOB-002E.description:
The 1888 obituary: the 'merchant of death' verdict into a seven-year testament project—31 million kronor entrusted to a fund he could not oversee—history's most famous reading of one's final judgment in advance
Modern drill: Crisis PR, upgraded: treat reviews and litigation papers as requirements documents—reconcile clause by clause and write compensable items into institutions (refund rules, safety standards), not press statements

C-NOB-003E.title: Nobel's 'Capital-Entrustment Method' applied today
C-NOB-003E.description:
The device of the 1895 will: 'realizable estate into safe securities into a fund, interest split five ways'—frozen principal, five-way allocation, three-body judging, complete on one page
Modern drill: The modern foundation: the endowment model of the Gates Foundation, Wellcome Trust, and peers—perpetual principal, earnings for programs—the direct descendant of capital entrustment

C-NOB-004E.title: Nobel's 'Remorse-Conversion Method' applied today
C-NOB-004E.description:
The Norwegian design of the Peace Prize: the supreme judgeship of peace handed to Norway's union-opposed parliament—replacing self-praise with an interest-opposed structure, the will's sharpest clause
Modern drill: Corporate ethical remediation: polluter remediation trusts, public-health-directed tobacco settlement funds—upgrading the apology statement into a permanent, interest-opposed appropriation structure

C-NOB-005E.title: Nobel's 'Control-Variable Method' applied today
C-NOB-005E.description:
Finding the cap (1863): charge and vessel fixed, initiators tried one by one—black powder, guncotton eliminated until the critical design, the primary charge pressed in a metal tube, was isolated
Modern drill: Clinical medicine: the single-intervention design and staged release of randomized controlled trials—the foundation of modern drug safety

C-NOB-006E.title: Nobel's 'Global-Deployment Method' applied today
C-NOB-006E.description:
Hamburg (1865): the first Nobel company in Germany—the first landing ground where kieselguhr supply, rail-and-mine demand, and patent protection all met
Modern drill: Multinational pharma: patent families laid jurisdiction by jurisdiction and local JVs completed before generic cliffs—the modern textbook of the patent cadastre

C-NOB-007E.title: Nobel's 'Patent-Moat Method' applied today
C-NOB-007E.description:
The three rings of 355 patents: core formulation, process detail, claimed uses—the Ohlsson brothers' 'improved explosive' hit Nobel's prior filings at every step
Modern drill: The smartphone patent wars: Apple versus Samsung, a decade of portfolio against portfolio—no single sheet ever decided the fight; network size was the leverage

C-NOB-008E.title: Nobel's 'Deterrence-Peace Method' applied today
C-NOB-008E.description:
'My factories may end war sooner than your congresses' (1890s): the full primitive statement—extremized destruction makes war suicide and reason stands down
Modern drill: The nuclear deterrence regime: MAD, second strike, hotlines—the full modern implementation of Nobel's function, cracks of the rational-actor assumption included

C-NOB-009E.title: Nobel's 'Symbolic-Award Method' applied today
C-NOB-009E.description:
The legislative bundle of five (1895): physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, peace on one stage—a checklist definition of 'human benefit,' the ordering legislated in a stroke
Modern drill: Academic honors: the Turing and Fields and Lasker prizes—inheriting the triple of checklist legislation, ritual fossilization, externalized judging

C-NOB-010E.title: Nobel's 'Cross-Domain Self-Cultivation Method' applied today
C-NOB-010E.description:
The five-language youth: barely a year of schooling before seventeen, five languages mastered through tutors and self-study—cross-domain self-cultivation beginning where no institution could be relied upon
Modern drill: Parallel reading and writing for technologists: Feynman's drawing and drumming, programmers writing fiction and reading philosophy—a second coordinate system against engineering's monopoly on judgment

C-AND-001E.title: Andersen's 'Small-Figure-Ennobling Method' applied today
C-AND-001E.description:
The Tinder Box (1835): a soldier mocked by a carriage-driver wins everything with one tinder box—'help me carry her down,' and the three dogs deal with princess, king, and queen in turn, until the whole town hails the soldier as king: a direct swap of the bottom and the crown
Modern drill: Content craft: the rise-hook of short video and web fiction—press the protagonist to the bottom in the first thirty seconds (fired, mocked, bankrupt) while giving the reader the information gap of 'who truly deserves'; retention runs on awaiting the moment the world flips

C-AND-002E.title: Andersen's 'Thing's-Eye-World Method' applied today
C-AND-002E.description:
The Darning Needle (1846): the complete life of a self-styled noble sewing needle from the needle-case to the gutter—it misreads each rescue as 'being appreciated' and dies not knowing it is a broken needle: the first-person specimen of vanity
Modern drill: Brand communication: let the product speak—a parcel box's self-account, an umbrella's monologue, an old phone's farewell letter; the thing's eye naturally dodges the bragging register and carries brand warmth more credibly than ad copy

C-AND-003E.title: Andersen's 'Suffering-Distillation Method' applied today
C-AND-003E.description:
The Little Match Girl (1845): four matches, four visions, one embrace from grandmother—Andersen distills 'frozen to death in the street' into the metaphysical close of 'no one knew what beautiful things she had seen,' the origin text of suffering's aesthetics in world literature
Modern drill: Content craft: a dignity-narrative discipline for real suffering—neither exploiting misery nor sweetening it; pair each pain with one visible exchange of beauty (a smile, a small kindness), so readers leave carrying light, not suffocation

C-AND-004E.title: Andersen's 'Child's-Eye-Truth Method' applied today
C-AND-004E.description:
The Emperor's New Clothes (1837): the curse 'invisible to the stupid' makes a whole city perjure itself—until the child's single sentence 'But he has nothing on!' delivers the tale's only speech of truth, while the emperor 'walked more proudly than ever': the complete anatomy of a collective lie
Modern drill: Organizational diagnosis: a meeting tool for the 'elephant in the room'—institute a 'child's question' slot where the most junior member may ask 'but why do we...,' with management guaranteeing it costs nothing

C-AND-005E.title: Andersen's 'Death-in-Soft-Light Method' applied today
C-AND-005E.description:
The Little Match Girl (1845): the New Year's sun shines on the girl frozen with a smile, burnt matches in her hand—'no one knew what beautiful things she had seen': the full weight of a miserable death redeemed clause by clause by 'having seen'
Modern drill: Death-education picture books and child communication: scripts for 'a pet has died' and 'saying goodbye to grandpa'—borrowing Andersen's four disciplines: never deny the death, swap the sensory channel (flowers at the funeral, not black cloth), give a direction (a place in memory), keep the voucher (a list of things done together)

C-AND-006E.title: Andersen's 'Wander-Metamorphosis Method' applied today
C-AND-006E.description:
The Ugly Duckling's three lodgings (1843): farmyard (original misrecognition), the hen-and-cat cottage (functional terms: lay eggs or purr), the lake (developed by the reflection in kindred eyes)—the full wander-metamorphosis series
Modern drill: Study abroad and cross-cultural growth: recast 'acculturation' as a chain of lodgings—stay in each culture until its terms collide with your nature, and let identity develop in the eyes of a community that truly understands you

C-AND-007E.title: Andersen's 'Oral-Music-Weaving Method' applied today
C-AND-007E.description:
The Little Mermaid's lift-off (1837): 'Far out at sea the water is blue as petals…'—an opening-line launch plus oral repetition ('so blue,' 'so deep') weaving musicality; the page carries a teller's voice
Modern drill: Podcasts and audio content: the tell-before-writing workflow—tell it once to real people, note their reactions, then script; the read-aloud test as final review

C-AND-008E.title: Andersen's 'Papercut-Improvisation Method' applied today
C-AND-008E.description:
Cutting and telling unified in the parlor (1840s-70s): when guests called he cut first and unfolded at the end—the unfolding landing on the story's last sentence; hundreds of papercuts share imagery with the tales (swans, dancers, duckling-like birds)
Modern drill: Design and product: prototype before outline—build a low-fi artifact you can hold and let form and requirements grow from one root, replacing spinning meetings

C-AND-009E.title: Andersen's 'Lowly-Self-Audit Method' applied today
C-AND-009E.description:
The two autobiographies (1846/1855): the cobbler father's illness and death, the mother's washing and drinking, the grandfather's madness all entered into the books—a systematic offense against the era's dignity-laundered memoir
Modern drill: Therapy and coaching: account-izing impostor syndrome—break 'do I deserve this' into concrete cases, reconciled item by item (evidence, counter-evidence, calibration), instead of a global verdict

C-AND-010E.title: Andersen's 'Tears-in-Laughter Method' applied today
C-AND-010E.description:
What the Old Man Does Is Always Right (1861): the chain of ever-worsening trades raises a laugh at each exchange, while the tale's heart is the marital trust behind 'whatever he does is right'—laughter and tears in one bottle
Modern drill: Film and television: the tragicomedy formula—Chaplin telling poverty through pratfalls, The Grand Budapest Hotel telling diaspora in candy colors; scenes designed so laugh and ache land on one beat

C-KIE-001E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Indirect-Communication Method' applied today
C-KIE-001E.description:
Either/Or (1843) published under the editor 'Victor Eremita': readers must adjudicate Don Juan versus Judge Vilhelm alone—no page answers for them
Modern drill: Coaching and question-based management: never hand subordinates the answer; design retrospectives where the problem exposes itself—the answer belongs to the one who works it, doubling the loyalty of execution

C-KIE-002E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Three-Stages Method' applied today
C-KIE-002E.description:
Kierkegaard returns Regine's ring in 1841: the painful leap from the aesthetic sphere (Copenhagen's wittiest wooer) to the ethical—cost: the burning of a whole love; yield: fourteen years of writing
Modern drill: Life-strategy consulting: sphere-diagnosis first—the client's complaint is not a problem but a misplacement of sphere; locate before prescribing, and never treat aesthetic emptiness with the ethicist's overtime plan

C-KIE-003E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Anxiety-as-Vertigo Method' applied today
C-KIE-003E.description:
May 1843, Kierkegaard writes from Berlin: 'I have just realized that I have been anxious all my life, and the anxiety is my strength'—the anonymous narrator's Berlin journey in Repetition is philosophy's finest experimental log of anticipatory anxiety
Modern drill: Existential therapy: Rollo May's The Meaning of Anxiety is built on Kierkegaard throughout—'anxiety reappraisal' is the first framework for career transitions, reproductive decisions, and crises of faith

C-KIE-004E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Despair-Diagnosis Method' applied today
C-KIE-004E.description:
The 'Pascalian despair' of The Sickness unto Death: a perfectly respectable person running wholly by social rules, diagnosed by Climacus as unconscious despair—'he does not know his disease's name, and the not-knowing is the condition'—respectability itself is the symptom
Modern drill: Intake in counseling: replace the coarse depression/anxiety split with the two-axis typology—fleeing-type clients get direction first, propping-type clients get 'the right to fail' first; a mis-aimed prescription worsens the condition

C-KIE-005E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Leap-of-Faith Method' applied today
C-KIE-005E.description:
The broken engagement of 1841: between 'universal happiness' (marriage, family, respectability) and a mission without reasons he chose the latter—'she wept, I wept, but I must go my way'—Fear and Trembling is the cipher of this event
Modern drill: Major career choices: when 'no defensible reason, yet unwilling to let go' appears, treat it as leap-grade—stop adding rows to the pros-and-cons table; design the silence period and the review checkpoint instead

C-KIE-006E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Single-Individual-First Method' applied today
C-KIE-006E.description:
The Corsair affair of 1846: caricatured for months, mocked by the whole city, he never retracted 'the public is a phantom'—the method's pricing experiment: the isolation cost paid in full, the proposition survived
Modern drill: User research: institutionalize the singular veto of the deep interview—mean reports must carry one named user's testimony; on conflict, pause the launch before investigating

C-KIE-007E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Irony-as-Clearing Method' applied today
C-KIE-007E.description:
29 September 1841, defense and broken engagement the same day: The Concept of Irony academically clears the ironic tradition after Socrates, and the same day he clears his own marriage prospects—thesis and life as each other's execution
Modern drill: Teaching and seminar: the operating protocol of the Socratic seminar—the instructor plays ignorant throughout, clarification questions only; grading measures not rightness but 'has the stance been loosened by its own holder'

C-KIE-008E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Subjective-Truth Method' applied today
C-KIE-008E.description:
The Postscript's praying contrast: the worshipper with a defective conception yet burning 'is subjectively nearer the truth'—the original locus of the 'rich in doctrine, poor in life' critique
Modern drill: Leadership audit: the consistency check of 'what you say' against 'how you live'—your team does not read your values wall; it reads your calendar and your bills

C-KIE-009E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Pseudonymous-Stratification Method' applied today
C-KIE-009E.description:
Either/Or's drawer narrative: the editor Victor Eremita claims to have found two stacks of manuscripts in a hidden desk compartment—before the stances even contend, 'authorial authority' has been replaced by an editorial board
Modern drill: Debate-format content: persona division in podcasts and columns—each stance has a resident voice (with its weakness), and the host is barred from concluding on the audience's behalf

C-KIE-010E.title: Kierkegaard's 'Melancholy-Distillation Method' applied today
C-KIE-010E.description:
The four-stage distillation of the broken engagement: the 1841 rupture → 'my Regine' in the diaries → Johannes of The Banquet → the 'knight of silence' of Fear and Trembling—one raw material pressed into four forms of increasing objectivity over twenty years
Modern drill: Disciplined writing therapy: upgrade 'journaling for catharsis' to a form requirement—each session must yield something shaped (a thousand-word essay, a poem draft); emotion labels alone are barred

C-YSS-001E.title: 地利锁喉法 scenario 1
C-YSS-001E.text: Drag the competitor into an alley its org chart cannot enter: in the RFP, raise the customization weight so the giant's standard product loses points

C-YSS-002E.title: 必死则生法 scenario 2
C-YSS-002E.text: Startup cash runway breaks: when persisting's expected value falls below liquidation-and-restart, dare to make liquidation the default and plan the core team's paths

C-YSS-003E.title: 残局重启法 scenario 3
C-YSS-003E.text: The company kills its flagship line: the remaining team does not petition to disband; it submits a list of 'the battles this establishment can still fight' with a deadline

C-YSS-004E.title: 龟甲奇器法 scenario 4
C-YSS-004E.text: Block the giant's core process with one directional patent: not field coverage, only 'making their default approach unusable'

C-YSS-005E.title: 乱中日记法 scenario 5
C-YSS-005E.text: Startup decision log: record 'the basis and expectation at the time' for every major call—your strongest self-evidence in financing litigation

C-YSS-006E.title: 鹤翼合围法 scenario 6
C-YSS-006E.text: Compete by dragging the giant into the single point where your whole line is ready—beat the resource gap with the simultaneity gap

C-YSS-007E.title: 忍谤续战法 scenario 7
C-YSS-007E.text: Workplace defamation: answer with deliverable records and email ledgers, not shouting—'still delivering' is the strongest statement

C-YSS-008E.title: 万全备战法 scenario 8
C-YSS-008E.text: Product launch: ship only when the release checklist is full to the mark—canary, rollback, monitoring, support scripts; the moment allows execution only

C-YSS-009E.title: 潮汐算战法 scenario 9
C-YSS-009E.text: Trading: build hour-level tables of rate decisions, settlement points, liquidity peaks—execute pre-set moves in the windows of reversal

C-YSS-010E.title: 孤忠担纲法 scenario 10
C-YSS-010E.text: Engineering safety: the senior engineer's bearing-veto against a dangerous launch—written stop, alternative plan, next quarter's delivery as the guarantee

C-SEJ-001E.title: Sejong's 'Daily-Use Encoding Method' applied today
C-SEJ-001E.description:
The promulgation of 1446—Wanting everyone to learn it easily and use it daily—the acceptance form holds no word for 'advanced,' only 'everyone' and 'daily use.'
Modern drill: Product design: before launch, write the acceptance test as one checkable sentence ('a first-time app user completes checkout in 10 minutes')—features that cannot state it are cut

C-SEJ-002E.title: Sejong's 'Local-Verification Method' applied today
C-SEJ-002E.description:
Straight Talk on Farming—There are Chinese methods that cannot work in our country—books may be copied, land may not; every conclusion counts only after local verification.
Modern drill: Cross-border expansion: a local validation period before entering a market—headquarters' growth model is a hypothesis until local data arrives

C-SEJ-003E.title: Sejong's 'Institution-as-Incubator Method' applied today
C-SEJ-003E.description:
Daily audiences in the Hall of Worthies—Talent unfostered does not come, and without it nothing is accomplished—I decline to be the genius; I will be the grid for geniuses.
Modern drill: Founder's note: externalize the knowledge that lives only in your head into institutions—process, archive, lineage; the company passing a two-week founder vacation is the test of construction

C-SEJ-004E.title: Sejong's 'Minimal-Script Method' applied today
C-SEJ-004E.description:
The anatomy of ㄱㅁㅅㅇ—Fewest symbols, widest coverage—each letter's shape is its own manual; learn the rule and every letter is already in your hand.
Modern drill: API design: a minimal consistent rule set generates every endpoint—learn one rule, use ten endpoints, beats twenty rules for twenty endpoints

C-SEJ-005E.title: Sejong's 'Tiered-Encoding Method' applied today
C-SEJ-005E.description:
1444, petitions accepted in hangul—One law, two canons—classical for the literati, vernacular for the people; governance is precise not when written deep but when decoded by its receiver.
Modern drill: Policy release: one policy, three versions—legal text / field-execution handbook / public Q&A—parallel canons with semantic-equivalence review

C-SEJ-006E.title: Sejong's 'Immune-Damping Method' applied today
C-SEJ-006E.description:
Choe Manri's memorial preserved in full, Sejong rebutting clause by clause—Being besieged is not danger but proof of work—I need not the critics' silence, only that their reaction fails to stop the project's advance.
Modern drill: Technology adoption: draft an immune-source list before shipping a radical feature—those whose jobs automation threatens get transition paths, not persuasion decks

C-SEJ-007E.title: Sejong's 'Populace-as-Gauge Method' applied today
C-SEJ-007E.description:
The Joryak reform of 1431—The ruler of the people cannot but first know the people's affairs—'the people as the root' must become the rice price, the disaster, the case file in a monthly report before governing begins.
Modern drill: Product operations: decompose 'user satisfaction' into monthly variables (retention, complaint rate, time-to-first-order)—the operator reads raw data directly, no paraphrase

C-SEJ-008E.title: Sejong's 'Combinatorial-Generation Method' applied today
C-SEJ-008E.description:
Syllabic assembly—I give you not infinite characters but twenty-eight letters and the rules of assembly—the rest of the sentences, you will grow yourselves.
Modern drill: Software architecture: Unix-style small tools, microservices—each service one thing, composition rights to the business side

C-SEJ-009E.title: Sejong's 'Engineering-Archive Method' applied today
C-SEJ-009E.description:
The Explanations and Examples—Delivering the letters is not finishing; delivering 'why they are made this way' is—only when the archive is written does the project first become immortal.
Modern drill: Software engineering: ADR + README + changelog—'why designed so' ships with the code

C-SEJ-010E.title: Sejong's 'Succession-Foreshadowing Method' applied today
C-SEJ-010E.description:
Three lines buried at promulgation—I do not hope my successors are wise; I bury into the project all the conditions for beginning again—the institution advancing, the principles on paper, the people's fingers already remembering.
Modern drill: Open-source governance: the BDFL retirement roadmap—foundation (institution) + complete docs (paper) + community habit (users), three lines buried

C-HCM-001E.title: 深耕耐心法 scenario 1
C-HCM-001E.text: Write unmonetizable-within-five-years capabilities into a personal budget: fund the 'ten-year rule' skills separately so quarterly metrics cannot kill them

C-HCM-002E.title: 地下组织法 scenario 2
C-HCM-002E.text: Key-person risk in a startup: back up and document every critical function—the founder's vacation is the organization's stress test

C-HCM-003E.title: 自我批评法 scenario 3
C-HCM-003E.text: Managerial retrospective: in the weekly meeting report your own misjudgments and corrections before the team's—the highest reviews first

C-HCM-004E.title: 人民动员法 scenario 4
C-HCM-004E.text: Cold-start for a community product: ship something immediately useful before community creed, with participation entries designed by user identity

C-HCM-005E.title: 文明自辩法 scenario 5
C-HCM-005E.text: Workplace rights: quote the Code of Conduct verbatim in the appeal, then reconcile item by item with concrete cases

C-HCM-006E.title: 文化借力法 scenario 6
C-HCM-006E.text: Brand communication: borrow public cultural symbols (solar terms, classics) and localize them into standing assets

C-HCM-007E.title: 朴素生活法 scenario 7
C-HCM-007E.text: Organizational culture: remove visible perks—reserved parking, executive dining—making 'no privilege' an institutional standard

C-HCM-008E.title: 实用弹性法 scenario 8
C-HCM-008E.text: Startup pivot: separate mission from product—the product may pivot while the mission stays constant in the funding narrative

C-HCM-009E.title: 化名身份法 scenario 9
C-HCM-009E.text: Creator operations: layer legal name, pen name, and handles; keep symbol names two or three syllables, memorable and ideal-bearing

C-HCM-010E.title: 民族和解优先法 scenario 10
C-HCM-010E.text: Post-merger integration: declare 'the original team is retained if not resisting' with joint-governance posts, converting hostile human capital into stock assets

C-SUK-001E.title: 最低共识法 scenario 1
C-SUK-001E.text: Drafting a cross-party charter: translate each side's non-negotiables into one elastic clause all can sign, deferring precise adjudication until an adjudicator exists

C-SUK-002E.title: 抓窗速决法 scenario 2
C-SUK-002E.text: Competing in an organizational gap: when a manager departs or a project goes vacant, make the smallest existing fact (public result, public commitment) so later allocation addresses what already exists

C-SUK-003E.title: 演讲造国法 scenario 3
C-SUK-003E.text: Organizational cold start: before budget and institutions, use the founder's consistent narrative and a fixed ritual (weekly all-hands) to create common belief

C-SUK-004E.title: 平衡互锁法 scenario 4
C-SUK-004E.text: Corporate governance: triangular checks among founder, capital, and professional management—with the pivot-exit structure preplanned

C-SUK-005E.title: 议程造势法 scenario 5
C-SUK-005E.text: Industry influence: a small team originates its own standard and summit, turning 'taking a seat' into 'setting the table'

C-SUK-006E.title: 符号工程法 scenario 6
C-SUK-006E.text: Brand cold start: design logo, naming system, numbered mnemonic, and anniversary rites in one pass; avoid fragmented symbol accretion

C-SUK-007E.title: 多元缝合法 scenario 7
C-SUK-007E.text: Unifying a multilingual team: choose a lingua franca avoiding the largest faction's mother tongue; write 'the whole is indivisible' into the charter's non-negotiable layer

C-SUK-008E.title: 道义联盟法 scenario 8
C-SUK-008E.text: Bargaining across platforms: hold a named, programmatic third-party position of 'no side' while keeping substantive ties with all bidders

C-SUK-009E.title: 指导收敛法 scenario 9
C-SUK-009E.text: Crisis centralization: a strong CEO's concentration must bind performance consideration and exit clauses—otherwise it is self-authorization

C-SUK-010E.title: 失衡警示法 scenario 10
C-SUK-010E.text: Unicorn audit: keep a 'narrative-cashflow' dual ledger with separate warning lines for symbolic expansion (launches, acquisitions)

C-MARQ-001E.title: 细节信托法 scenario 1
C-MARQ-001E.text: Remedios the Beauty's ascension: all the ink on the physical detail of the sheets; the miracle completed in the shape of a household accident.

C-MARQ-002E.title: 宿命先行法 scenario 2
C-MARQ-002E.text: The opening sentence of One Hundred Years of Solitude: one sentence fixing past, present, and future—the most famous sentence in twentieth-century fiction.

C-MARQ-003E.title: 集体视角法 scenario 3
C-MARQ-003E.text: Chronicle of a Death Foretold: nearly all three thousand in town knew; the narrator's 'we' draws the reader into the conspiring chorus of witnesses.

C-MARQ-004E.title: 采访考古法 scenario 4
C-MARQ-004E.text: The sailor report (1955): three weeks, six hours a day, reconstructing ten days adrift hour by hour—reportage that enraged the junta and forced exile.

C-MARQ-005E.title: 荒诞对冲法 scenario 5
C-MARQ-005E.text: The banana massacre: three thousand dead, two hundred freight cars, official denial, communal forgetting—plain news style, zero magic, the book's most terrifying passage.

C-MARQ-006E.title: 时态织造法 scenario 6
C-MARQ-006E.text: The tense magic of the opening: facing the firing squad (future)... was to remember (looking back from that future)... that distant afternoon (the past of the past)—three layers in one.

C-MARQ-007E.title: 孤独书写法 scenario 7
C-MARQ-007E.text: Seven generations of Buendías: alchemy, the gold fish, retreat from love—the same mechanism of solitude recurring until love's birth deciphers the parchment.

C-MARQ-008E.title: 关系复利法 scenario 8
C-MARQ-008E.text: The detonation of One Hundred Years: the Boom camp's joint backing (including the young Vargas Llosa)—decades of writer-circle maintenance redeemed at once in 1967.

C-MARQ-009E.title: 入世斡旋法 scenario 9
C-MARQ-009E.text: The M-19 talks (1989-90): carrying messages between guerrilla leaders and top officials on bilateral friendship, seeing the guerrillas lay down arms and become a legal party.

C-MARQ-010E.title: 魔幻警示法 scenario 10
C-MARQ-010E.text: The Nobel lecture (1982): itemizing Latin American realities on the world's highest literary podium—'do not judge us by literary standards'—the inventor puncturing his own label.

C-BORG-001E.text: Your convoy must cross a fog-sealed sea; the log records twelve previous flotillas with different ends—some rounding the storm, some wrecked, some lost. The old bosun wants the familiar route forced; the first mate wants to anchor. Applying the forking-time method, you do not pick one path: you build three branches, marking on each the confluence events that happen whatever you choose (tides, supplies) and the true fork points (the last turn before the storm zone), and order the navigators a signaling plan that lets branches communicate. When the fog lifts on the third day, you sail with a walked fork-map—the universe as a perpetually forking novel, applied to navigation.

C-BORG-002E.text: Intelligence reports the enemy cipher comes from a machine 'impossible to exhaust'; intercepts are an ocean. You invoke the arithmetic of the Library of Babel: every cipher machine has a generating alphabet and a mechanism; 'inexhaustible' only means unfinished enumeration. You order the cryptanalysis team to make no guesses in week one—confirm the character set, compute the permutation count and mechanical period, estimate the share of valid plaintext—then filter only the highest-share channels. In three weeks the mechanism is derived. You remind them: the infinite is only the permutation of a finite set; once the arithmetic is done, the absurd becomes enumerable too.

C-BORG-003E.text: Marketing wants the founder's twenty-year-old internal letter ('we do not chase scale, we chase being singular') as the new strategy's slogan, quoted verbatim. You note that meaning is a function of words × situation × era: when it was written the firm was near bankruptcy and scale was a threat; today scale is the opportunity. You require the situation-triplet be annotated and the founder to rewrite what the same words mean in the new situation—letters nearly unchanged, meaning explicitly re-anchored.

C-BORG-004E.text: You must educate a market on an entirely new category, with a budget far too small to explain all the principles. The white paper does not argue; it is built in scholarly grammar—an evidence chain citing three real third-party test reports (real carriers), parameters annotated to page-level retrievability, with one deliberate small discrepancy between two pages of charts, publicly corrected. Customer research shows the correction notice significantly raises credibility. You tell the team: the highest form of credibility is not true content but unassailable form—and detecting evidence too perfect is also the lesson in not being deceived.

C-BORG-005E.text: The board deadlocks on owning logistics: one camp heavy-asset, one light-asset. Instead of a vote you run the paradox-pair method: each side writes the dual-consequence list of the other's plan (how heavy dies when demand contracts, how light dies when capacity is squeezed) and pushes the pair to its exchange point—under what conditions the heavy camp would envy the light, and vice versa. Finally a third concept, cash-flow endurance, breaks the antinomy into a decidable practical question: set the endurance threshold first, then choose.

C-BORG-006E.text: Your research team makes a controversial methodological breakthrough; the juniors want co-byline publicity. You apply the anonymity-of-tradition method: the result is credited to the laboratory tradition, technical details lodged in 'internal memoranda,' individuals saying only 'one step of ten years' work.' When the storm comes six months later, it falls on the method, not persons; the team revises calmly, and next year, confirmed, the traditional byline lets every successor inherit the honor. You repeat Borges: personal fame is high-liability; the book outlives the man.

C-BORG-007E.text: You must write the strategy paper for a new division, but the environment shifts so fast any concrete plan is stale in six months. You use subtraction-toward-infinity: the paper does not plan; it writes 'the structure of that plan'—the division's generating alphabet (three core capabilities, two customer classes, one cash constraint), three explicitly excluded paths, and testimony on 'what different scenarios would read into it.' At review, each business lead generates their own version in the blank, all conforming to the interface. You quote Borges: I pretend the plan already exists, and then I comment upon it.

C-BORG-008E.text: The reporting system shows metric self-reference inflation: new KPIs set to hit KPIs, measured by next quarter's new KPIs—reflection out of control. Using the mirror-maze method you first locate the layer describing the system itself (the KPI stack as the organization's mirror), then ground it—every self-referential metric must anchor to an externally unmanipulable physical quantity (retention, cash, yield), distinguishing authentication-type self-reference (kept) from inflation-type (cut). The metric layer halves, every metric traceable to a physical quantity in two steps.

C-BORG-009E.text: Your team is fluent in two disciplines (machine learning and clinical medicine) but each speaks its own jargon and meetings idle. You run terminology-alignment sessions on the bilingual-confluence method: both sides back-translate core concepts, flagging 'words that will not cross' ('overfitting' has no home in clinical language) and opening a project on each homeless word. Three months later the team poses two new questions neither discipline alone could have asked. You quote Borges: the homeless word is the genuinely new concept.

C-BORG-010E.text: The company suddenly loses its main sales channel (a platform ban); morale collapses; some want to buy the channel back at any price, others to imitate competitors wholesale. You run the four steps of the blindness-convergence method: inventory undamaged assets (private-domain users, product strength, cash), confirming a channel—not a capability—was lost; build a new production line on the private domain (community, live commerce, membership) instead of forcing platform logic; register the constraint as style—products emphasizing deep service over traffic hits; and tell everyone plainly: there is no return to the old life; the new stage has its own classics. Six months later the new channel's margin exceeds the old.

C-NER-001E.text: Scenario drill (misread critical proposal): a project lead facing misread critical proposal decides to apply Neruda's Material-Translation Method. Step one, translate each abstract demand into checkable particulars—finding every item its 'material equivalent.' Step two, draw the situation's geographic map, giving each unit a place and a voice; material that fits no voice is cut. Step three, revise by two tests—'can it be passed from hand to hand' and 'will readers raise their hands.' Step four, choose constant material signs and let them arrive before declarations at every major occasion. At the close, the audience both feels named and leaves holding a tangible thing—the direct application of Neruda's Material-Translation Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-SHA-001E.text: Scenario drill (radical questioning in a new field): a project lead facing radical questioning in a new field decides to apply Shankara's Non-Dual Reduction Method. Step one, reduce or build the strongest opponent—ask of the object in succession 'on what does it stand' until the unfailing ground, or reconstruct the other side's position to the strongest form their own camp would nod at. Step two, check levels and adjudication—most conflicts are level-mismatch, not factual error; higher truth does not cancel lower obligation, and lower experience does not overstep to refute. Step three, close with apophasis and realization: define the undefinable by excluding what it is not, mark every remaining conclusion as hypothesis, and design a repeatable verification procedure. Step four, turn results into institutions: prerequisite checklists, a teachable ladder and redundancy that does not depend on any one person, so the results keep generating after anyone leaves. At the close, the audience holds both a checkable record of exclusions and verifications and a structure with no single point of anchorage—the direct application of Shankara's Non-Dual Reduction Method in a contemporary work setting.
