C-NAG-001E.text: Scenario drill (auditing essentialist discourse): a project lead facing auditing essentialist discourse decides to apply Nagarjuna's Dependent-Origination-as-Emptiness Method. Step one, put the dependence question to the object: 'does it stand by itself, or on causes, parts and concepts?'—list its conditions of dependence.  Step two, apply the dilemma: if it has intrinsic nature it needs no arising and admits no change, contrary to experience; if it arises depending on conditions, it lacks intrinsic nature.  Step three, complete the reversal: declare that emptiness does not abolish the object but names its absence of intrinsic nature, and that only thus are its causal efficacy and knowability possible.  Step four, close by self-consumption: hand emptiness itself back to dependence, never to be reified as a highest truth.  At the close, the audience holds both a checkable list of conditions of dependence and an explanatory structure resting on no frozen essence—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Dependent-Origination-as-Emptiness Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-002E.text: Scenario drill (enumerating options before a major decision): a project lead facing enumerating options before a major decision decides to apply Nagarjuna's Tetralemma-Refutation Method. Step one, formalize the question as a proposition and enumerate its four positions: P, not-P, both, neither.  Step two, derive a reductio from each position's own premises: holding 'is' cannot explain change; holding 'is not' undermines itself; 'both' is self-contradictory; 'neither' still takes is/is-not as its coordinate.  Step three, declare that the conclusion is not a fifth position but that 'propositions of this type cannot ultimately hold'—the question is dissolved, not answered.  Step four, run the self-consumption check: examine whether a thesis has been smuggled in; if 'all is empty' is held as a thesis, apply the tetralemma to emptiness itself.  At the close, the audience holds both a record of four-corner reductios and a critical structure occupying no position—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Tetralemma-Refutation Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-003E.text: Scenario drill (governing titles and designations in an organization): a project lead facing governing titles and designations in an organization decides to apply Nagarjuna's Dependent-Designation Method. Step one, run the designation test: strip away all conceptual imputation—what remains? If the answer is another layer of imputation, the object is pure designation.  Step two, map the designation's conditions of dependence: on which parts, conventions and contexts the name stands—trace its lineage.  Step three, exclude both ways: the substance the name denotes is neither outside the name nor inside it; designation and referent relate by dependence, not identity or separation.  Step four, establish as needed: retain and use the designation conventionally while marking its lack of intrinsic nature—use without clinging, which is the middle way.  At the close, the audience holds both a lineage table of designations and a naming standard of use-without-clinging—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Dependent-Designation Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-004E.text: Scenario drill (arbitrating scientism against humanistic values): a project lead facing arbitrating scientism against humanistic values decides to apply Nagarjuna's Two-Truths Stratification Method. Step one, identify which level each side stands on: mark every proposition as conventional operation (agreement, practice, institution) or ultimate operation (intrinsic-nature scrutiny).  Step two, rewrite the 'emptiness vs. being' dispute as level-mismatch: one side refuting conventional propositions with the ultimate, the other resisting ultimate scrutiny with worldly intuition—correct the level before debating content.  Step three, apply the ladder rule: any route to the ultimate must be built of conventional material, itself acknowledged as lacking intrinsic nature.  Step four, apply the non-voiding rule: after the ultimate conclusion, check item by item that worldly obligations still hold—only reifying clinging is cancelled, not obligation itself.  At the close, the audience holds both a level-marking checklist and an adjudicating structure whose levels never cancel each other—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Two-Truths Stratification Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-005E.text: Scenario drill (diagnosing organizational reification): a project lead facing diagnosing organizational reification decides to apply Nagarjuna's Identity-Difference Dissolution Method. Step one, identify the dependent pair: agent-patient, whole-part, role-competence—name both sides.  Step two, test identity: if the two are one, do their stations and functions vanish?—usually yes (role and person merge, structure collapses), so identity fails.  Step three, test difference: if the two are utterly unrelated, can the dependence still hold?—usually not (apart from people the role idles), so difference fails.  Step four, remove the reification: declare 'the relation is real, the substantial bearer is not established'—keep the relation working conventionally while refusing to read it as two or one intrinsically-natured things.  At the close, the audience holds both a record of one/different tests and a relationally established view of organization—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Identity-Difference Dissolution Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-006E.text: Scenario drill (the four-gate audit of success attribution): a project lead facing the four-gate audit of success attribution decides to apply Nagarjuna's No-Arising Argument Method. Step one, decompose the causal claim 'X arises from Y' into four structures: X pre-exists in Y (self), X differs in intrinsic nature (other), both combined, no cause needed.  Step two, run reductio at each gate: self-arising produces nothing and regresses; other-arising entails anything-from-anything; both fails doubly; causeless collapses causation and effort.  Step three, declare the conclusion with all gates shut: no arising—not a denial that events occur but of the reading 'an intrinsic thing is produced'; success is re-established as a convergence of conditions.  Step four, pair with the two truths: keep every everyday use of 'achievement' conventionally while marking its lack of intrinsic nature—so the audit is not read as denying effort.  At the close, the audience holds both a four-gate reductio record and a humble dependence-based structure of attribution—the direct application of Nagarjuna's No-Arising Argument Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-007E.text: Scenario drill (designing a third axis between polarized policies): a project lead facing designing a third axis between polarized policies decides to apply Nagarjuna's Middle-Way Practice Method. Step one, formulate the conflict as a pair of extremes: plan/market, centralize/devolve—state both poles' terms.  Step two, hunt the shared presupposition: what unexamined premise do both share? (usually 'one correct institutional ontology exists').  Step three, abandon the presupposition, not one pole: declare both poles untenable on the 'sole correctness' axis and establish action on the design of conditions of dependence.  Step four, carry into practice: in norms (rules valid as conditioned designations) and in action (a participating condition within a convergence), enact the stance of dependence.  At the close, the audience holds both a shared-presupposition analysis and a scheme design beyond the poles—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Middle-Way Practice Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-008E.text: Scenario drill (designing sunset clauses for management tools): a project lead facing designing sunset clauses for management tools decides to apply Nagarjuna's Emptiness-of-Emptiness Method. Step one, identify the system's top-level concept: the most central, least negotiable word on which the method rests (say, 'OKR,' 'agile,' 'digital transformation').  Step two, audit the concept's imputation structure: on what opposite or context does it stand?—find its 'standing on the non-empty' counterpart.  Step three, execute the self-consumption: show that when the system's goal is achieved, the top-level concept loses its opposite and its referent—it must be laid down with the situation.  Step four, install a sunset clause: write 'this tool is discarded after use' into the institution itself, with a standing reminder against second-order clinging (the discarding becoming a new dogma).  At the close, the audience holds both a tool-retirement clause and a self-renewing governance structure—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Emptiness-of-Emptiness Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-009E.text: Scenario drill (cooling position-proliferation in meetings): a project lead facing cooling position-proliferation in meetings decides to apply Nagarjuna's Prolificulation-Ceasing Method. Step one, recognize proliferation: check whether discussion endlessly spawns positions on a few axes (right/wrong, gain/loss)—the symptom is 'new positions breeding on old ones.'  Step two, locate the driver: ask 'which possessiveness does this concept game serve?'—a debate to win, a position defended; behind proliferation there is always clinging.  Step three, loosen the clinging, not the concepts: change the incentives (whoever concedes first scores), unbind identity, so proliferation loses its fuel—do not fight the words, cut the supply.  Step four, verify cessation: proliferation has stopped not when 'no views remain' but when views no longer breed—one still speaks and acts, but every sentence is a tool, not a new position.  At the close, the audience holds both a clinging-driver analysis and a supply-cutting design of meeting governance—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Prolificulation-Ceasing Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-NAG-010E.text: Scenario drill (designing a founder's gratitude closure): a project lead facing designing a founder's gratitude closure decides to apply Nagarjuna's Gratitude-and-Transmission Method. Step one, at completion separate 'innovation' from 'stewardship': state explicitly what is inherited and what is unfolded—return the method to its source tradition and take the position of steward, not legislator.  Step two, replace self-coronation with gratitude rites: open and close the system with tribute and dedication texts, directing attention from 'author' to 'transmission chain.'  Step three, lay multi-path transmission: train successors in person, commit the work to circulation, so the system depends on no single carrier.  Step four, rehearse the exit: stage 'the person may go, the system endures' for posterity—the founder's exit posture is itself part of the system.  At the close, the audience holds both a transmission roadmap and a closure structure resting on no single person—the direct application of Nagarjuna's Gratitude-and-Transmission Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-001E.text: Scenario drill (delivering a landmark result across generations): a project lead facing delivering a landmark result across generations decides to apply Padmasambhava's Terma-Concealment Method. Step one, assess the moment of reception: can the audience digest the full form now?—if not, weigh the cost of force-delivery.  Step two, choose the sealing carrier: write the finding into a durable, system-symbiotic medium—texts, objects, geography, custom or members' minds.  Step three, pre-designate the unlocking protocol: by whom, when and upon what signs it may be opened—the unlocker verifiably bound to the carrier.  Step four, authorize self-keeping: after sealing, do not micro-manage—hand the finished work to a future already written.  At the close, the audience holds both a sealed document with unlock conditions and a transmission structure that needs no one present—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Terma-Concealment Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-002E.text: Scenario drill (fitting communication across a multicultural organization): a project lead facing fitting communication across a multicultural organization decides to apply Padmasambhava's Affinity-Adaptation Method. Step one, diagnose the audience: map their existing system—beliefs, customs, fears, language—locating the untouchable base and the reusable structures.  Step two, choose enlistment or bypass: enlist what can be reassigned (keep the form, change the function); bypass rather than confront the rest.  Step three, stratify by capacity: write the one core at different densities, each layer independently valid and pointing to the same core.  Step four, verify the core survives: after any restatement, check the core claim still holds—adaptation changes clothes, not the person.  At the close, the audience holds both a capacity-diagnosis sheet and a communication architecture of invariant core and layered forms—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Affinity-Adaptation Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-003E.text: Scenario drill (priming one's state before a critical negotiation): a project lead facing priming one's state before a critical negotiation decides to apply Padmasambhava's Deity-Yoga Identification Method. Step one, select the archetype: choose a model by target mental state (the bold for courage, the calm for poise)—the archetype as a personified index of the capability.  Step two, enter under control: with a fixed ritual set the boundary of identification (time, space, posture) and generate the archetype's mental state item by item.  Step three, act within identification: handle real affairs from that state (talks, decisions, crises)—behavior changes before character.  Step four, exit in stages: ritually dismantle the identification and record which states were brought out—keeping the self from being swallowed by the role.  At the close, the audience holds both a state-priming operation card and a become-first-act-second capability acquisition routine—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Deity-Yoga Identification Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-004E.text: Scenario drill (designing dual tracks for a research organization): a project lead facing designing dual tracks for a research organization decides to apply Padmasambhava's Dual-Track Institution Method. Step one, identify the unmergeable pair: confirm exploration and delivery are both necessary yet mutually constraining—adjudication would kill one.  Step two, design the shared base: fix first what both tracks share (admission, values, terminology, destination)—differences at the method level, not the goal level.  Step three, install the promotion gate: state the qualification and selection for moving between tracks—the gate is the only insurance against misuse.  Step four, calibrate the tracks periodically: a mechanism with representatives of both, preventing two tracks from becoming two camps.  At the close, the audience holds both a dual-track rights-and-duties matrix and an organization standing its foundation and summit side by side—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Dual-Track Institution Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-005E.text: Scenario drill (handling the loudest opposition by conscription): a project lead facing handling the loudest opposition by conscription decides to apply Padmasambhava's Wrathful-Subjugation Method. Step one, assess the opponent's energy: gauge scale, source and mobilization logic—subjugation presumes real energy, not 'ignorance.'  Step two, switch to the stronger form: without leaving your value core, activate the most deterrent form they can perceive—calibrated to make them stop, not perish.  Step three, channel into a controlled track: the moment they stop, offer a new post (a role within the rules, a share of gains)—deterrence ends in conscription.  Step four, fix as load-bearing structure: bind the conscripted party's interests to the system's survival—'opposing you' permanently costlier than 'working for you.'  At the close, the audience holds both a conscription-post design and a governance scheme turning threat into load-bearing structure—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Wrathful-Subjugation Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-006E.text: Scenario drill (designing tiered access for a high-risk system): a project lead facing designing tiered access for a high-risk system decides to apply Padmasambhava's Empowerment-Gatekeeping Method. Step one, rate the capability's danger: assess harm radius and reversibility—danger class sets the number of tiers and gate strength.  Step two, design tiered keys: decompose the capability into grantable levels, each with its training, license and operating range.  Step three, bind signed responsibility: every grant carries its usage boundary and consequences—the newly capable learn responsibility's full weight at the moment of grant.  Step four, install continuous compliance: periodic re-checks, revocation and peer oversight—licenses 'currently valid,' never 'permanently held.'  At the close, the audience holds both a tiered permission matrix and a gatekeeping system conferring capability and responsibility together—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Empowerment-Gatekeeping Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-007E.text: Scenario drill (navigating a major organizational transition): a project lead facing navigating a major organizational transition decides to apply Padmasambhava's Bardo-Navigation Method. Step one, enumerate the transition's stages: decompose the change (merger, relocation, layoffs) into successive stages with recognizable signs for each.  Step two, pre-write per-stage guidance: three lines per stage—'what you will see,' 'what it is,' 'what to do now'—brief and executable.  Step three, rehearse in full while stable: everyone reads the whole script and drills the key moves, putting the script into procedural memory.  Step four, appoint the on-scene guide: in transition a guide prompts stage by stage, holding pre-authorization for each action.  At the close, the audience holds both a transition navigation manual and a mechanism rehearsing unknown panic into known action—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Bardo-Navigation Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-008E.text: Scenario drill (reworking talent review around what is already there): a project lead facing reworking talent review around what is already there decides to apply Padmasambhava's Direct-Pointing-of-Dzogchen Method. Step one, confirm it is innate: examine whether the capability is truly already present rather than manufacturable—if not, switch to training.  Step two, create occasions, not lectures: design moments for people to see for themselves they already have it (release after pressure, a pointing question)—pointing at seeing, not studying.  Step three, confirm on the spot: have them confirm 'just this, now'—specifically, preventing mistaking a lucky episode for the capability.  Step four, shift to guarding: after recognition change modes—no new knowledge added; design the daily that keeps it (brief frequent re-recognitions, triggers, peer checks).  At the close, the audience holds both a capability-confirmation record and a recognize-first-then-guard talent development routine—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Direct-Pointing-of-Dzogchen Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-009E.text: Scenario drill (writing a founder's exit memorandum): a project lead facing writing a founder's exit memorandum decides to apply Padmasambhava's Prophetic-Exit Method. Step one, switch document type at exit: routines go to institutions; only the future risks and turns institutions cannot cover enter the prophecy.  Step two, write a risk list, not a promise list: the body is 'what bad things will happen'—pre-immunization against bad news outranks anticipation of good news.  Step three, leave a 'profile slot' for successors: describe the needed person by recognizable traits—direction without locking a name.  Step four, design the fulfillment-confirmation procedure: agree in advance what counts as fulfillment and who confirms—otherwise prophecy degenerates into arbitrary interpretation.  At the close, the audience holds both an exit prophecy document and a closing scheme of risk pre-announcement plus successor profiles—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Prophetic-Exit Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-PAD-010E.text: Scenario drill (closing a system with attribution and entrustment): a project lead facing closing a system with attribution and entrustment decides to apply Padmasambhava's Gratitude-Entrustment Method. Step one, run a contribution-attribution audit: itemize which shares of the fruits belong to lineage, collaboration, circumstance and oneself—the audit itself counters deification.  Step two, rewrite the texts in source-returning narrative: 'I invented X' becomes 'following my lineage's X, unfolded in this new terrain'—facts kept, authority structure changed.  Step three, design the entrustment contract: successors take over as executors, not heirs, with keeping conditions and re-transmission duty.  Step four, close with gratitude rites: homage texts at the system's opening and end—every future reading an act of source-return.  At the close, the audience holds both an attribution audit and entrustment contract and a transmission structure resting on no single person—the direct application of Padmasambhava's Gratitude-Entrustment Method in a contemporary work setting.

C-AUR-001E.text: Scenario drill (auditing the source of an emergent new thing): a lead facing an audit of where a sudden 'new thing' came from decides to apply Aurobindo's Involution-Evolution Double-Pass Method. Step one, interrogate the 'emergent new': is it truly ex nihilo or the awakening of something already present?—trace its involutionary deposits, listing which potentials long slept in place.  Step two, rebuild the double-pass ladder: situate the current state in both directions—out of which layers it involuted, toward which layers it may evolve.  Step three, project the next station: since each layer sleeps on the potential of the next, ask 'what still sleeps in the depths of the current layer'—write transitionality as a structural position.  Step four, book the resistance: identify the 'dark forces' on the emergence path (inertia, atavism, chance) so the doctrine of direction does not become a painless progressivism.  In the end the audience holds both a self-checkable inventory of involutionary deposits and an explanatory structure that does not mystify the new—this is Aurobindo's Involution-Evolution Double-Pass Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-002E.text: Scenario drill (a stage deliverable being blamed as a defect): a lead whose stage output is being held up as a defect decides to apply Aurobindo's Transitional-Being Positioning Method. Step one, refuse the finished-product assumption: before judging the current state, run the three questions of process positioning—from what did it evolve, at which station does it stand, what is the next station.  Step two, rewrite the attribute labels: turn the 'defect list' into a 'work-in-progress list'—separating 'normal incompleteness of this stage' from 'problems that truly block the next station.'  Step three, reset the criteria: rewrite 'is it good now' as 'does it favor the next emergence'—ranking and choosing by evolutionary position, not static perfection.  Step four, install a delivery constraint: bound the 'transitional'—each station must carry present obligations and a stage deliverable, so 'on the way' cannot become infinite deferral.  In the end the audience holds both a choice list re-ranked by evolutionary position and an evaluation structure that refuses to stigmatize the unfinished—this is Aurobindo's Transitional-Being Positioning Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-003E.text: Scenario drill (a one-pass push at the total goal failed): a lead whose single drive at the grand goal has failed decides to apply Aurobindo's Triple-Transformation Staging Method. Step one, write out the total goal explicitly and concede it 'unexecutable in one pass'—stating why a single leap is insufficient (which layers a leap cannot reach).  Step two, divide the ascending levels: let each level solve one slice of the total goal, defining its entrance (how to enter), chief obstacle (how it fails) and completion test (what counts as cleared).  Step three, declare sequence and dependency: make explicit which levels must precede which, and the known risks of skipping—writing 'non-skippable' as protocol, not advice.  Step four, set verification and delivery points: each level gets observable stage deliverables, the total goal long-range milestones—keeping the aim undiluted while making progress testable.  In the end the audience holds both a level-by-level verifiable transformation roadmap and a staging structure that forbids discounting the goal—this is Aurobindo's Triple-Transformation Staging Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-004E.text: Scenario drill (rival routes deadlocked): a lead facing a standoff among competing routes decides to apply Aurobindo's Integral-Synthesis Method. Step one, inventory what each party truly sees: list the real facet each competitor holds—granting every party its local correctness before speaking of synthesis.  Step two, find or build the higher unifying structure: which framework can house all parties?—if none exists, legislate a new one (as 'the evolution of consciousness' housed science and spirit).  Step three, write the division-of-stations rule: what each party is responsible for in the unified structure, its boundaries, its hand-offs—'each at its station' must answer 'when does this party yield.'  Step four, test for enlargement: does the synthesis yield a new goal or capability none of the parties could give alone?—an 'integration' without enlargement has fallen back into juxtaposition; ascend a level again.  In the end the audience holds both a division map with every party at its station and a structure that grades synthesis by its enlargement yield—this is Aurobindo's Integral-Synthesis Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-005E.text: Scenario drill (a high-level result that will not land): a lead whose elevated achievement stays upstairs decides to apply Aurobindo's Descent-Verification Method. Step one, identify the system's densest layer: ask 'where is change hardest'—bodily habit, the organization's routine procedures, financial cash flow; locate the point of maximal resistance.  Step two, project the higher achievement onto the dense layer: what traces should it leave there?—writing out the concrete observable changes (behaviors, procedures, numbers).  Step three, run the trace test: inspect the dense layer on the ground—zero traces, or traces visible only upstairs, means 'high but not descended'; record the result as 'experience,' not 'attainment.'  Step four, plan the descent work: design the downward route for the higher achievement (which carriers, which steps bring it into the densest layer), and accept the dense layer's degree of rewriting as the final acceptance.  In the end the audience holds both a trace-test record for the densest layer and an acceptance structure that refuses to mistake upstairs clarity for landed completion—this is Aurobindo's Descent-Verification Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-006E.text: Scenario drill (the team arguing across levels): a lead facing a team dispute where nobody stands on the same level decides to apply Aurobindo's Consciousness-Level Mapping Method. Step one, expand 'consciousness/capability' into an explicit layer map: list the layers (at minimum: habitual execution—analysis—intuition—panorama) and write each layer's mode of operation.  Step two, locate the present difficulty at a layer: which layer does this problem essentially belong to, and with whose tools is it being handled?—identify the layer mismatch.  Step three, consult the layer's failure-mode library: what typically fails at this layer (over-reduction at analysis, over-certainty at intuition)—guard against in-layer failure before considering ascent.  Step four, decide between ascent and effort: is the problem 'solvable within the layer but hard' or 'unsolvable within the layer'?—the former calls for effort, the latter for ascent; and design the transition path upward.  In the end the audience holds both a layer map with its failure-mode library and a decision structure that reclassifies 'cannot think it through' as 'standing on the wrong layer'—this is Aurobindo's Consciousness-Level Mapping Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-007E.text: Scenario drill (the enterprise stalling when the founder leaves): a lead facing a break in the enterprise at the founder's exit decides to apply Aurobindo's Action-Yoga Entrustment Method. Step one, run the dependence audit: how much of the old enterprise's success now depends on irreplaceable personal input?—if the critical path can be carried by others and the trend, document the grounds.  Step two, design the sealing structure: convert the enterprise to a self-sustaining state 'continuable by others, completable by the trend'—naming the entrusted objects (people, institutions, the spirit already instilled), leaving nothing suspended.  Step three, legislate the turn: ground the pivot in a higher priority or calling (stated clearly inwardly and outwardly), declaring 'not abandonment but entrustment' to preserve the old enterprise's nominal value.  Step four, move the asset list: inventory the transferable skills, networks and reputation from the old work and wire them explicitly into the new—so the turn is not a net loss.  In the end the audience holds both an entrustment inventory with nothing left suspended and a sealing structure that turns without forfeiting prior work—this is Aurobindo's Action-Yoga Entrustment Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-008E.text: Scenario drill (influence fading after stepping back): a lead whose influence fails after moving off the front line decides to apply Aurobindo's Silent-Force Method. Step one, design the silent channels: before leaving the front stage, build the structures that keep working in absence (written principles, periodic rites, circulate-able letters)—so 'withdrawal' is not 'severance.'  Step two, preset the intervention criteria: write down which order of event must break the silence (existential, principled) and in what capacity one speaks—institutionalizing the 'exception' against both speechlessness and abuse.  Step three, build the organizational firewall: the silent influence must not travel through organizational interest—keeping personal principle and institutional stance separate to preserve the influence's purity and credibility.  Step four, execute with restraint: silence is the norm, the trigger the exception—review each trigger against the preset criteria before and after, lest the 'exception' swell into a 'new normal.'  In the end the audience holds both an intervention protocol triggered only by criteria and a contingency structure that makes the退场者's absence deeper rather than louder—this is Aurobindo's Silent-Force Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-009E.text: Scenario drill (the new system lacking foundations): a lead whose new framework lacks grounding decides to apply Aurobindo's Dialogical-Synthesis Method. Step one, select the strongest interlocutors: for each structural unit to be built, find the interlocutor representing the strongest tradition of that facet—never entangling with weak hands.  Step two, respond whole-length, not in footnotes: organize one's text by the interlocutor's problem structure (commentary, chapter-by-chapter response, dialogue form)—placing the dialogue in load-bearing position.  Step three, run absorptive responses: judge each item of the other's 'true facet' and 'price'—absorbing the facet, refusing the price (taking materialism's felt realism while refusing its cancellation of consciousness).  Step four, test the load-bearing: remove the interlocutor and see whether one's structure still stands—any member wholly dependent on the other needs internal grounding against the aging of foundations.  In the end the audience holds both a response ledger of 'facet absorbed / price refused' and a construction that survives the interlocutor's removal—this is Aurobindo's Dialogical-Synthesis Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-AUR-010E.text: Scenario drill (the cause scattering as the founder exits): a lead facing the dissipation of the cause at the founder's withdrawal decides to apply Aurobindo's Human-Unity Closure Method. Step one, pre-inscribe the personal goal into the whole-aim: define 'what trans-personal vision my work finally serves' and argue the isomorphism of individual perfection and the whole-aim—so the enterprise is larger than the person by design.  Step two, build de-personalized institutions: descend the aim into runnable institutional form (community, foundation, charter) with an explicit 'belongs to nobody' clause.  Step three, lay multi-carrier transmission: texts, successors and rites in parallel, so the system survives the loss of any single carrier—a redundant design for transmission.  Step four, rehearse exit-as-takeover: make each carrier's operation independent of the founder's presence and regularly test 'does the system run with the founder absent'—exit is takeover.  In the end the audience holds both a three-line redundant transmission structure and a closure mechanism whose acceptance test is 'the founder absent'—this is Aurobindo's Human-Unity Closure Method applied directly to a contemporary work scenario.

C-MAI-001E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-001E.text: A cross-regional legal-aid network faces a two-thousand-page casebook: divergent rulings on like cases scattered everywhere, new lawyers unable to find purchase. Applying Maimonides's gathering method, they first re-cut and classify all precedents by 'the client's life-stage and objects of duty,' write each entry as a self-contained loop (definition—rules—borderline cases), adjudicate one current conclusion for each contested point with its authority grade marked (consensus/majority/private judgment), and finally strip the historical discussion, keeping only the ruling. Three months later a new lawyer can practice from any single entry. The cost then shows: the excised history of debate was the very material that trained judgment, and a senior partner complains 'a code does not grow jurists.'

C-MAI-002E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-002E.text: A global open-source community has argued for three years over 'what counts as a compliant contribution,' splitting in two and bleeding contributors. The governance group, following Maimonides's creedal extraction, tests every dispute by 'does rejecting its conclusion threaten the project's survival,' and extracts seven numbered bottom lines (true attribution, license compatibility, verifiable supply chain), declaring all else 'outside the list and freely arguable,' and matching instruments to sources of dispute: internal splits decided by data and argument, external attacks answered by apologetics from premises the opponent accepts. The controversy converges within a month. Six months later comes the backlash: items on the list are misread as 'settled and beyond question,' forcing the group to add a procedure for revising the list itself.

C-MAI-003E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-003E.text: An AI lab convenes a definitional summit on 'alignment': each positive definition proposed ('obey human intent,' 'harmless,' 'beneficial') is instantly gamed by the red team—just as Maimonides said, every added predicate adds a misidentification. The team switches to the negative method: excluding item by item 'what alignment is not' (not compliance sign-off, not harmless output, not instruction-following, not a values score), each exclusion sealing one family of exploits, and the unexcludable remainder is registered as a provisional statement of direction with an explicit confession that 'this cannot be finally defined.' Safety assessment is henceforth measured by progress of exclusion, not completeness of definition.

C-MAI-004E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-004E.text: A century-old company's charter reads 'the founder shall forever preside,' clashing with the fact that the founder is dead. The board adopts Maimonides's three gates: fix the unshakables first (the statutory governance structure, the founder's written behests), test each clause for conflict—the literal sense of 'preside' as bodily presence is irreconcilable with the established fact, so controlled decoding opens; decoding proceeds by priority (the whole intent of the behests before the isolated phrase), rereading 'preside' as 'the founder-approved governance mechanisms continue to operate,' with the decoding ground and 'why literal possibility fails' marked in the resolution. When shareholders sue, that audit trail is the key evidence that interpretation was no one's fiat.

C-MAI-005E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-005E.text: An executive famed for violent decision-making takes on character calibration. The coach refuses unmeasurable goals like 'become gentler' and switches to Maimonides's coordinate method: positioning 'decisiveness' between recklessness and timidity with a written midpoint test (no major decision overnight, capable of being talked back by new evidence, ten minutes capped for small ones), re-measured weekly alongside the midpoint test for anger (only on matters that greatly warrant it, capable of being talked back down). The first two months, while the coordinate would not hold, use overshoot training—deliberately delegating for two weeks, then correcting back. At the quarterly review the tests show the coordinate stabilized—except humility toward his own errors, carved out under the exception clause: cultivated to the utmost low, never held at the middle.

C-MAI-006E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-006E.text: A gene-editing research platform is caught in serial conflicts of 'technical feasibility vs. ethical baseline': every experiment application becomes total war among the whole staff. The governance layer first draws the jurisdictional map (fact-layer to research review, ought-layer to the ethics charter), then fixes the three steps: reread the clauses for misreading→seek a third option distorting neither data nor charter→failing that, act on the baseline and register the open question. The weighting rules are fixed in advance: where decidable, demonstrated data outranks intuitive literalism; in the ought-layer the charter's authority is untouched by technical conclusions. A year later conflict processing falls from weeks to days, and the 'undecidable list' becomes a formal agenda source for charter revision.

C-MAI-007E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-007E.text: A telemedicine platform suffers chronic follow-up failure: doctors prescribe by 'disease name' in three minutes, and patients fail at home. The platform adopts Maimonides's three features: intake opens a variable file (constitution, dwelling climate, work rhythm, sleep, state of mind), prescriptions are issued by variable-combination ('same disease, different prescription' becomes institutionally normal), interventions are ranked with regimen first (food/sleep/exercise/mood prescriptions before drugs), and a subordination-to-jurisdiction clause is written in—the on-call physician never suspends response for holidays, and professional ethics outrank platform performance metrics. Within six months follow-up failure drops by forty percent, and 'emotional variables' become a standard prescription field.

C-MAI-008E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-008E.text: A distributed open-source foundation falls into governance crisis: members across four continents, the executive director's directives read as power-grabs, and in-person mediation covering only one time zone. The foundation adopts Maimonides's epistolary arbitration: every major decision written as a three-part document (situation diagnosis→charter grounding→directives with deadlines and boundaries), registers chosen by need—communities seeking consolation get diagnosis and empathy first with rulings slowed, contributors seeking adjudication get the law directly. Groundings are always cited to charter clauses anyone can independently verify. Three months on, 'diagnosis-free' directives fall to zero, and the documents are accepted directly by third-party arbitrators—authority executed without bodily presence.

C-MAI-009E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-009E.text: A language-learning company faces the distortion of 'mastery' marketing: users claim fluency while tests say otherwise. The curriculum adopts Maimonides's asymptotic ladder: 'mastery' rewritten as a program of infinite approximation with self-checkable per-rung differences (excluding one typical misunderstanding, completing one class of real-scenario tasks), motives trained in grades from interest-driven to object-driven (for the exam→for understanding→for the language itself), with the summit declared open and self-overestimation hedged (each rung carries the self-check 'you may have overestimated your rung'). Completion rises, and 'mastery' is removed from the marketing vocabulary—the company begins pricing by rung-gaps rather than attainment.

C-MAI-010E.civilization: The Jewish civilization of the medieval Islamic west (the Andalusi-Maghrebi-Egyptian diaspora axis): halakhic ruling, persecution and exile, interfaith scholarly context
C-MAI-010E.text: A methodology consultancy's manual goes unexecuted: nods in training, nothing in practice. The partners turn to Maimonides's exemplar-closure: the methodology's four domains (decision, writing, client communication, internal research) gathered into the partners' own publicly verifiable lived practice—meeting notes, decision logs, records of declined clients, all open internally; with the declaration made in advance that 'character controversies and propositional truth are audited separately,' and the trade-off costs written down (hours lost to holding offices, revenue from clients refused). Two years later the manual's execution rate passes half—the new hires imitate 'how this person lives,' not 'what the manual says'.

C-SUL-001E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-001E.text: A multinational retail chain is drowning in a rule war between store standards and national regulation: the headquarters manual and local custom clash, regional managers improvising at will. Following Suleiman's dual-track codification, the governance group first draws the boundary—the group charter (the sharia analog) holds only non-negotiable values and red lines, while the operations code (the kanunname analog) turns commission, liability and scheduling into numbered articles reverse-engineered from 'what each region actually does'; the two tracks join in a regional operations committee, with precedence at collisions backstopped by the group's tradition of justice and written into the text. A year later a new regional manager can open a store from any single article. The cost then shows: the code ratifies existing practice, and the experimental stores complain 'the manual locks out experiments'—the conservative order of retroactive codification is endogenous to the institution.

C-SUL-002E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-002E.text: An open-source foundation inherits three incompatible communities (developers, designers, educators), each wanting to rewrite governance in its own culture. Following Suleiman's layered-millet method, the foundation cuts units by 'community' rather than 'issue'—each community self-governs internal affairs by its own code of conduct, while the foundation retains only two services: cross-community arbitration and infrastructure security; the appointment of each community's lead is reserved to the foundation (headman hostage), with autonomy and escalation lists written into the charter in advance. Conflict drops within the quarter. Two years later the seam shows: one community translates 'communal identity' into 'an exclusive club,' and cross-community contribution dies between two layers of approval—the high cost of layered governance for boundary-crossing individuals stands exposed.

C-SUL-003E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-003E.text: A fast-scaling tech firm is paralyzed by veteran factions: early employees' equity and networks turn the executive meeting into a factional bazaar. Following Suleiman's bonded-elite ladder, the CEO restricts new executive hiring to cross-regional talent with zero ties to local factions, adds dense common training and rotation (the taming layer), and rewrites equity terms—promotion framed as 'a grant of the board,' not desert, with buyback clauses and honorific titles binding property and identity to the firm. Within two years factionalization reverses. Five years on comes the recoil: when the CEO semi-retires, the bonded executives instantly turn from 'the king's servants' into contenders in a power vacuum—the channel's loyalty points at the person, not the institution.

C-SUL-004E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-004E.text: A cloud vendor fights for developers with 'free quota plus cash subsidies': three years of burn leave the cash flow desperate, and users bleed the moment subsidies stop. Following Suleiman's fief-timar method, the firm converts 'quota' into 'a trust of the tax stream'—resources registered and granted by a team's service grade (commitments, migration depth), the grant priced against annual committed spend, idle use downgraded and recalled, a central register making the fiscal archive the sales mobilization table. Eighteen months after the swap from subsidy to credit, cash flow turns positive. In year four the market peaks, new quota stops flowing, and the contracts begin systematic default: incumbents trade grants privately, idle users refuse release—the blood-cut moment of the self-circulation, word for word the timar's decline in the histories.

C-SUL-005E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-005E.text: An auto giant's EV transition is stuck at 'launch first, organization lagging': the EV unit burns cash yearly while R&D and channel structure still tilt to combustion. Following Suleiman's sea-pivot method, the new CEO first diagnoses negative marginal returns (three years of shrinking combustion margins), then re-charters by the new domain's core mission—the EV is no longer 'an extension of the car' but a product line defined as 'energy service'; meanwhile the founder of the industry's strongest independent charging network is absorbed whole with his team as its head (co-optive absorption), and pivot quotas are assigned to finance and HR alike. Three years on the transition takes shape. The price shows in step: the absorbed unit drifts toward regency, and budget and oversight design become a perennial governance task.

C-SUL-006E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-006E.text: The industry's number two launches a total price war against the leader: a year later both are bloodied and its cash flow wrecked. The new strategy chief adopts Suleiman's Habsburg-buffer method of dimension-lowered management—the decision-battle abandoned: 'client products' sponsored for standoff in the leader's adjacent category; the leader's internal channel contradictions inventoried, with formal joint programs signed with two of its big distributors (the wedge document); adversarial spending written as institutionalized action 'by budget, by cycle,' with demonstrative deterrence (precise counterstrikes in chosen markets) replacing total conquest. Two years later the leader sues for peace. The lesson is recorded too: one deterrence operation was read at home as 'capitulation'—the accounting unit of deterrence and of politics never shared a currency, and narrative pre-scripting became standard equipment that day.

C-SUL-007E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-007E.text: A legacy manufacturer mid-restructuring: the rules changed, the hearts did not—new processes pushed purely by administrative order. Following Suleiman's poet-jurist co-regency, the chairman opens two legitimacy accounts: the pen of institutions issues process and accountability under the real name (the decree account), while the pen of culture serializes a transformation narrative in 'love letters to the workshop' style under a byname in the house journal (the Muhibbi account); double patronage follows—funding the veteran masters' technical-authority classroom (the in-system interpreters) and the young engineers' vanguard retrofit projects (the frontier creators) alike, staged to endorse each other at the plant's anniversary; 'quality is dignity' is written into the new plant's spatial design (geometry as rhetoric). Two years later the processes run by themselves. The hazard is planted in step: the byline column loses its measure after the chairman retires, and a successor's imitation becomes satirical material—the balance of the two pens hangs on the pen-holder.

C-SUL-008E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-008E.text: In a family firm the founder's spouse has long acted as a 'shadow CFO' swaying financial decisions: elders resent it, heirs distrust it, and all influence runs in the dark. Following Suleiman's consort-in-government method, the board abandons the fantasy of removal and turns to housing design: the spouse receives a formal standing (head of the family foundation), with influence steered into public, checkable functions—external philanthropy, the employee welfare fund, education of the next generation (functional institutionalization); appointments and budgets disclosed quarterly to the board (auditability); with a handover clause written in advance stating 'this mandate binds the person, not the seat.' Within three years shadow politics vanishes. The hazard arrives on schedule: at the second generation the handover clause is challenged as 'outdated'—the distinction between de facto power and seat-right becomes a permanent topic of the family constitution.

C-SUL-009E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-009E.text: A city's community-library system fights for budget every year: one fiscal squeeze shuts a third of the branches. Following Suleiman's pious-foundation method, the Friends of the Library lift the public good out of the fiscal cycle: a trust of perpetual title in a row of street-level shops is endowed (rents as budget), the charter states 'use unalterable, assets unsellable,' locked by local public law rather than contract (the sacred lock); donors trade naming and board seats for perpetual repute (repute-binding), with external audit and succession rules pre-set. Ten years on the libraries stay open through three squeezes. The shadow accumulates in step: the retail strip declines and rents sag for years—the price of dead-hand property surfaces: assets that cannot be sold are perpetual on the wrong use.

C-SUL-010E.civilization: Ottoman-Islamic civilization of the sixteenth century: imperial codification, layered plural governance, Mediterranean sea-power rivalry, waqf endowment and courtly cultural engineering
C-SUL-010E.text: A founder who took the firm from garage to IPO is near retirement: every institutional innovation (options, retrospectives, open-sourcing) lies scattered, with no transmissible identity-word. Following Suleiman's lawgiver-persona closure, he first inventories the institutional outputs and seeks the confluence—four streams (engineering standards, public retrospectives, apprenticeship, the refusal of option-gilding) all point to 'treating engineers as adults'; he pledges the institutions with the person: before retiring he publicly enforces the rules that bind himself (a personal share-lock clause, an open retrospective of his own three gravest mistakes); he refines the closure point into an identity-word, 'the Engineers' First' (not a slogan); and he pre-manages the attack surface—admitting the stain (one failed acquisition) rather than erasing it, hedging personal collapse with an independently audited institutional account. Ten years after retirement the identity-word is still endlessly reused across the industry's registers. The attack surface is struck in the end: his son's scandal pierces the icon for a season—but the institutional account's independence keeps the firm from falling with it.

C-SPI-001E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-001E.text: A consultant drafting a digital-transformation plan finds his conclusion-first deck repeatedly challenged with 'why should we trust you.' Rebuilding it by Spinoza's geometric closure, he first pins down every definition ('digitalization,' 'go-live,' 'success metric' each given one unambiguous sentence), then lists five premises all parties accept (axioms), and states each recommendation as a numbered proposition with its derivation chain. At the review, objections are for the first time localized to a specific step: someone rejects 'premise 2,' and the meeting stops comparing eloquence and starts checking premise 2's data source. The cost appears at once: a vice president says 'the definitions page is too cold, there's no vision'—the price of geometric form is the absence of feeling; the closer must also carry an 'appendix' to move people.

C-SPI-002E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-002E.text: A SaaS firm's data team finds 'customer' maintained inconsistently in CRM, billing and support. Following substance unification, the architect first sets the qualifying condition—'exists independently = can change its lifecycle independently'—then audits each definition's attribute set: billing's 'customer' is really a 'contract,' support's really a 'contact.' The deduction follows: one substance only; the rest are its modes under different states. Unifying storage turns the three systems into three views of one substance. Six months later the problem returns with 'order': someone insists 'order and order-line are two entities'—the proof binds only those who accept the definitions, and the quarrel over definitions forever reopens at the gate of the system.

C-SPI-003E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-003E.text: A founder, his core team having left together, is caught in a loop of remorse, replaying 'I should have kept them.' Running a necessity-settling review, he first separates 'the information and options available then' (the causal chain) from 'the outcome known only after' (imagination)—reclassifying remorse as residue of a passive affect; then extracts only causal knowledge: retention failed because of the option structure, not the conversations, and this enters the new company's terms. Three months later a core partner leaves again, and his reaction shifts from 'why me again' to 'which link is still unrepaired'—the emotion's intensity has not vanished, but its source has. The cost: an investor remarks he is 'too calm, as if it doesn't hurt'—one who understands necessity is easily misread as cold.

C-SPI-004E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-004E.text: A growth team argues endlessly over 'why users churn'—price, competitors, or 'the mystique of experience.' By the geometry of the passions they decompose churned users' emotion into the two base tones (gain rising or falling) and the object (product/self/others), then derive by class: 'feeling neglected' is 'declining gain directed at the platform'; 'anger' is that combination plus the imagination of a better alternative. Resources are allocated by composition, not complaint: one 'price' grievance, decomposed, is mostly 'wounded pride,' and the price-change plan is shelved. The cost: a user writes, 'you treat our feelings as a component table'—to geometrize emotion predicts behavior yet may spend empathy.

C-SPI-005E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-005E.text: A venerable publisher is to revise an editorial standard 'observed for thirty years.' The new editor, by the historical-grammatical method, first suspends the premise that 'the standard is authority' and treats it as a historical text—a ledger of issuance dates, shifts of wording across versions, citations among clauses. The examination finds: three clauses revered as 'founding principles' are emergency patches from a nineties mishap, while the true founding document is cited by no one. Revision proceeds 'by the text interpreting the text': ambiguous clauses decided only by the term's actual usage across all documents, with no back-pouring of 'original intent.' An objector demands, 'by what right do you abolish tradition?' He answers, 'I have not abolished it; I have dated it.' The cost: half a year of examination, far slower than rewriting by intuition—the historical method's price is time.

C-SPI-006E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-006E.text: A ten-thousand-member open-source community's governance group disputes whether 'political speech' warrants expulsion—one faction demands a total ban, another total license. By the free-state method they first establish the community's essence: its power is members' ceded share of force; it can govern repositories and conduct, never minds. The boundary follows: govern outward action (harassment, sabotaged builds), not inner judgment (views, stances)—permitted dissent stays inside the issue process; deleted opinion leaves with a martyr's halo to found a rival. The charter runs a year, no 'seceding party' appears, but a new problem does: certain views spill over into action (refusing to review some people's code)—the border dispute shifts from 'saying' to 'doing,' and the group finds a free polity is an interface requiring perpetual arbitration, not a one-time verdict.

C-SPI-007E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-007E.text: A product lead must decide the fate of an 'eternally hitless' aging product line. By the virtue-as-power method she first lays down the minimal principle: what is this line's striving—to persevere in being, or to rearise from a corpse? Then she translates 'ought' into 'power': each option assessed by 'whether it grows the team's long-run autonomy and capacity of action.' The data yields the counterintuitive verdict: shutting the line and folding the team into new business maximizes skill transfer—attachment to 'the hit we once had' is a pain-based affect (remorse fused with pride) generating no power. She decides: shut it, publishing the full derivation. The cost: an old engineer says at leaving, 'you turned sentiment into arithmetic'—the power audit improves the decision while spending the sense of meaning.

C-SPI-008E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-008E.text: An engineer finds he 'knows many microservice terms but cannot design,' and three courses bring no improvement. By the third-kind-knowledge method he first diagnoses his grade: the terms are signs and hearsay (first kind), the courses gave inference (second), but he has never tasted direct structural grasping (third). He rebuilds his study: every design returns first to common notions (the true definitions of consistency, availability, cost) and reasons from these to the concrete scheme; each completed system is repeatedly 'viewed from the most universal principles' until 'where it will break' becomes visible at a glance. Six months on, he reviews proposals markedly faster—not from more patterns but from compressing inference into intuition. The cost: in a new field (ML systems) his intuition is zero—the third kind cannot be rushed past the second.

C-SPI-009E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-009E.text: A freelance consultant is courted by three platforms for 'exclusive' contracts—generous, but each demands 'no public criticism of platform policy.' By the self-sufficiency method he first audits economically: does his current craft (independent consulting) require him to remodel his judgment? No—an exclusive contract does. He declines, and compresses his wants: three subscriptions dropped, the office shrunk, 'summit appearances' demoted from necessity to option. The fewer the wants, the smaller the surface where terms must be endured. Six months later the largest platform returns to the table accepting his right to criticize. The cost: a sly 'too proud for us' at an industry dinner, and the lean months truly sting—the arithmetic of self-sufficiency requires paying solitude's bill in advance.

C-SPI-010E.civilization: Dutch-Republic and early-modern European civilization of the seventeenth century: Amsterdam's relative toleration and commercial society, Cartesianism, the Sephardic diaspora, and the political-theological conflicts of the United Provinces
C-SPI-010E.text: A tech blogger, three years of fragmented 'tips,' has followers aplenty but hears his claims doubted: 'you don't live this way yourself.' Reorganizing by the system-as-person closure method, he first writes the methodology as one complete, testable system (definitions—premises—derivations), pausing publication to finish the whole; then he cashes every conclusion in life—'no recommendation without reasoning' answered by publishing all his affiliate income, 'minimize wants' by a public inventory of his devices and tools. Every claim ships with 'its counterpart event in my practice.' The challenge rate falls markedly—not because the prose improved, but because the person began to stand surety for the system. The cost: publication a year and a half late, while a competitor took the topic—the price of closure is setting the system's integrity above the speed of exposure.

C-TOU-001E.civilization: Mid- to late-twentieth-century Chinese science under state mobilization: the '523' national mission, the integrated Chinese-Western medicine policy, the herbal literary tradition, and the WHO-led global public health system
C-TOU-001E.text: An enterprise architecture team inherits a legacy system of dubious provenance: over a hundred functions of rumor-strength existence, no one able to say which are in use. The lead suspends the rewrite instinct and, following Tu Youyou's recipe-ledger method, builds a 'full-inventory ledger of functions'—logs scanned, veterans interviewed, even IT tickets and verbal agreements entered as numbered items. Three months on the ledger stands: 183 entries, 78 'confirmed in use,' 52 'conditionally ineffective' (idle since a channel retired). Screening proceeds by ledger layers, and the migration plan gains its first traceable basis. The cost shows in step: the cataloguing time is repeatedly challenged with 'why not just start'—the order of exhaust-then-act must be re-argued before every impatient stakeholder.

C-TOU-002E.civilization: Mid- to late-twentieth-century Chinese science under state mobilization: the '523' national mission, the integrated Chinese-Western medicine policy, the herbal literary tradition, and the WHO-led global public health system
C-TOU-002E.text: A content platform condemned 'invitation-code signup' as a failed scheme three years ago: the data read 'low conversion.' The new growth lead refuses to close the case and, like Tu Youyou re-auditing the Ge Hong entry, returns to the raw data word by word—the low conversion had occurred under 'cold start plus no identity endorsement,' while a competitor with the same mechanism converted threefold in the same period. The lesson is filed too: another buried feature, 'place check-in,' enters the re-test queue—it failed on 'no content pool,' and the platform now holds three years of content.

C-TOU-003E.text: A production line's yield slides from 97% to 89%; quality wants to replace the core material supplier. C-TOU-004E.text: A medical-device startup's flagship awaits three animal-study reports; an investor threatens to pull out unless 'humans within two weeks.' The cost is explicitly recorded: under modern regulation this stands only as a 'voluntary plus filing' supplement, never a substitute for the formal process—the person as surety has limits.

Field readings are written back into breeding targets, and only the second version rolls out the next year. The loop costs a year over the launch event, but it moves the rout from after rollout to before it.

C-RFR-008E.text: A senior risk expert tops out at her firm (a small temple, many talents) and chooses to leave. Inventorying her assets she separates data from method: the case files stay, but the entire method of 'reading fraud patterns out of transaction flows' goes with her. Her new employer's regtech is nascent and method-scarce — she enters with a mature methodology and within a year upgrades anti-fraud from a pile of rules to a recomputable model system, outranking her former post. The unit of migration is the method, not the topic.

C-RFR-009E.civilization: Postwar British science: women pushed into research posts by the war and back out of them after it; the tension between collective MRC research and individual credit; the civic tradition of a middle-class Anglo-Jewish family (a father who taught evenings at the Working Men's College and housed Kindertransport children); the crystallographic lineage of Cambridge and Birkbeck's Bernal school
C-RFR-009E.text: An architect gives her new hire only edge tasks; six months pass, no growth. She switches to mentor-peer: handing over the production-grade troubleshooting manual, her own list of habitual errors, and her standards of judgement, then letting the hire run one real on-call shift alone and sign one retrospective. Half a year later the hire owns one of her core subsystems and she is free for a new direction — the unit of inheritance is a recomputable method chain, not obedience.
