C-WCY-010E.text: A founder, knowing he will step down in five years, settles three things in advance: name the successor, write ten core principles no one may change, and set seven business leads each against a different segment. Five years on the company runs seven lines, four times the scale, values unchanged.

C-YLC-001E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-001E.text: Facing the proposal to empty the Han lands for pasture, Yelü Chucai folded an entire civilization into a revenue sheet: half a million taels, eighty thousand bolts, four hundred thousand shi. He never said 'letters must not perish'; he said 'run the numbers yourself' — to save a civilization, translate it into the conqueror's accounting language.

C-YLC-002E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-002E.text: The old Mongol way was sack the city, take the spoil. Chucai fixed land and trade taxes and set ten tax commissions — a paper stating the exact sum, taking from the army the power of 'take as we please'. The people learned for the first time what they owed; the court, what it would receive: the fixed rate itself is a civilization's promise.

C-YLC-003E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-003E.text: Princes contended before the throne for districts and households, each with his word. Chucai did not argue; he called for the registers and checked on the spot — what the book lacked was denied. He changed the contest from whose voice is louder to what the book says; the ledger became the only third party qualified to speak.

C-YLC-004E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-004E.text: Genghis Khan knew no classics but trusted the stars. Serving the western campaign with medicine and calendrics, Chucai spoke 'spare this city' inside an omen of Mars in warning — the same sentence, from a remonstrator it earns death, from a diviner it is adopted. The first step of counsel is not persuasion but finding the channel the other already trusts.

C-YLC-005E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-005E.text: Setting a gnomon on the walls of Samarqand, Chucai cross-checked the Chinese calendar against western measurements and issued a new reckoning. From then on tax days, document deadlines and assembly dates all hung on one official time — the most political thing he did for the empire was to solve the most technical question: what hour is it now.

C-YLC-006E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-006E.text: The steppe keeps its fiefs and road-judges; the Han lands their magistrates and taxes — Chucai demanded neither side become the other, but built the interface of tax commissions and ledgers above both rails. He did not make a uniform empire; he made a coordinated frame in which difference could live.

C-YLC-007E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-007E.text: Under the regency of Töregene, edicts flowed from outside the chancellery. Chucai no longer had the veto, but he still held the signature and the four words 'the late emperor's statutes' — every bad decree passed one more door, one step slower. A full veto was impossible; a stayed veto still vetoes.

C-YLC-008E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-008E.text: Of Khitan royal blood, schooled in Chan under Wan-song, serving Confucian in the Secretariat — as 'Juran Layman' he gave each tradition its place: Chan to steady the heart, Confucian way to govern, lineage as root. He lost himself in no identity, and used none to deny the others.

C-YLC-009E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-009E.text: 'A thousand autumns may hear the name only; one day's meeting endures forever.' Speaking to Genghis Khan, Chucai never pressed with morality but moved with the name after death — sparing the slaughter is not a favor to me; it is the lettering on your own monument. He made benevolent rule the conqueror's own image project.

C-YLC-010E.civilization: The Han lands and steppe under the Mongol empire of the 13th century — a Eurasian world of collapse, conquest and coexisting civilizations
C-YLC-010E.text: Every protection he won, Chucai wrote into statute, lodged in standing offices like the tax and compilation commissions, and staffed through examinations he held to raise successors. After his death his enemies wrecked his policies — but the papers stood and the precedent held: when Qubilai's court revived Han law, it took up the skeleton Chucai had folded into the institutions.

C-YZ-001E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-001E.text: The quota frozen in 1711, the poll silver yet yearly uncollectable: the poor fled, the rich shifted their names. Yongzheng set up no new tax and proclaimed no abolition — he moved three million taels whole into the land tax, spread by acreage. Much land, much due; no land, nothing. The two-thousand-year head tax came apart by one rescript, and the treasury not a tael lighter.

C-YZ-011E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-011E.text: Ministers urged delay, fearing the landed gentry. Yongzheng's arithmetic differed: the poll silver was an accomplished fact, frozen by Kangxi; merging it into acreage added nothing, only moved it. Reform borrowed a prior reign's momentum, demoting a thousand-year fiscal revolution to a bookkeeping operation.

C-YZ-002E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-002E.text: A governor's memorial, sealed, passed neither the forwarding office nor the grand secretariat, straight to the throne. Yongzheng annotated in vermilion by lamplight, sometimes hundreds of characters, down to grain prices and rainfall. The hierarchy showed him a PR-ed world, so he built an encrypted channel beside it — answering the blindness of power with the design of information.

C-YZ-012E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-012E.text: Governors, commanders, provincial judges all memorialized, none knowing another's contents. A viceroy might report all quiet, unaware three intendants had already told the truth of the matter — the cost of lying soaring because collusion was impossible. Trust is scarce; redundant corroboration is the rebar of any system.

C-YZ-003E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-003E.text: Military reports crossed thousands of li; grand-secretarial drafting lagged. Yongzheng lodged the Grand Council by the Longzong gate: a few councilors, a few rooms, no staff of its own. The lighter the organ, the more direct the grip, the smaller the leak — the heaviest power housed in the leanest frame, lean-fast-secret its entire manual.

C-YZ-013E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-013E.text: With the council standing, the grand secretariat ground on and the princes kept their titles — nothing was abolished, yet matters of state all flowed through the small rooms by the wall. Yongzheng knew the virtue of supersession by coexistence: abolishing an old office is political earthquake; standing a small one beside it is a mere administrative note.

C-YZ-004E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-004E.text: Meltage fees were the counties' private surcharge — how much 'loss' the silver's recasting cost was a matter of conscience and nerve. Yongzheng ordered each province a fixed rate, remitted to the treasury: arbitrary levies turned statutory overnight, gray income moving from the magistrate's purse to the public account.

C-YZ-014E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-014E.text: A governor's salary, barely a hundred taels; his nourish-honesty allowance, ten or twenty thousand — and Yongzheng never disguised that the source was confiscated gray income. Institutions must pay for integrity, he admitted: honesty turning from a moral demand into economic rationality, the greedy losing their pretext, the honest able to feed their houses.

C-YZ-005E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-005E.text: Ortai faced not a province but dozens of hereditary chieftains. He raised no army: entering through succession disputes and blood feuds, converting house by house, arbitration wherever it could serve, arms only as final endorsement — replacing chieftains with magistrates as a war waged with institutions, not swords.

C-YZ-015E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-015E.text: The day Wumeng converted, administrative takeover began: a removable magistrate, fields surveyed, taxes rated, schools opened for frontier children. The victory was worth a day; the conversion held because of the three legs after it — finance, registers, education. A color on the map becomes part of the state's structure only by becoming ledgers and primers first.

C-YZ-006E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-006E.text: One month into the reign, he named the treasury's deficits — millions, unpardonable, unvarnished. The audit house answered to the throne, not the treasury it audited; repayment pursued on deadline, princes and governors alike, estates stripped, even suicides' heirs reached. The new reign's first act was clearing, for every new institution must start from a clean ledger.

C-YZ-016E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-016E.text: Two kinds of deficit: borrowed for public ends, rescheduled; stolen for private ends, pursued to the end. A clearing is not one stroke — the nature of the debt sets the force, and discrimination is what lets recovery stand morally and proceed practically.

C-YZ-007E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-007E.text: Felling Nian Gengyao took two years: protégés transferred first, provincial chiefs quietly instructed to keep distance, then ninety-two counts of conviction — every step clothed in judicial process. Yongzheng's consolidations never went naked: statutory charges preceding political moves, each strike unassailable in procedure.

C-YZ-017E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-017E.text: When Nian fell, the northwest's civil and military administration was not swept with him: only the principal struck, his party split. The essence of pruning one by one is tempo, not sharpness — control the blast radius at each step, and the remaining vines each calculate alone instead of league together.

C-YZ-008E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-008E.text: Li Wei, a clerk who had bought his rank, reached governor-general in ten years. The official world cried out; the emperor answered in vermilion — seniority was never made for men of action. Reform needs the daring; the standard of selection precedes all procedure, and shielding the promoted from scorn is part and parcel of out-of-turn advancement.

C-YZ-018E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-018E.text: Every office matter logged with deadline, reported monthly, lateness penalized in pay and rank — a timetable nailed between 'assigned' and 'done'. Execution by Yongzheng was never slogans: after choosing the right man, let the system bite.

C-YZ-009E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-009E.text: In his first year the succession rescript, written in his own hand, was sealed behind the tablet of Brightness Upright — the choice made and unknowable, unworkable even by the heir himself. An open heir breeds a prince's party; no heir at all invites chaos: with secrecy he kept both certainty and stability at once.

C-YZ-019E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-019E.text: The night Yongzheng died suddenly, Zhang Tingyu and Ortai, acting on the duplicate rescript prepared in advance, enthroned the new emperor before dawn. The sealed system passed its harshest test: the handover no longer a trial of fists but one sealed page and a public rite. The institution ran for a century, and the wars of succession ended in the dynasty.

C-YZ-010E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-010E.text: Zeng Jing's charges — forced the father, drove the mother, slew his brothers — struck at the very legitimacy of the accession. Yongzheng met them head-on: interrogating the traitor himself and issuing the Record to the realm — an emperor descending to debate a rumor. Magnificent and fatal: palace secrets entered every schoolhouse, and the accusation traveled with the imperial edict.

C-YZ-020E.civilization: The court and eighteen provinces of the high Qing in the 18th century — a vast bureaucratic empire driven by memorials, tax ledgers and sealed caskets
C-YZ-020E.text: Qianlong, once enthroned, executed the lecturer and banned the Record, not a copy to survive. The father's open debate was judged too much exposure — an innovation against the successor's interest dies with its maker. Any high-visibility unconventional strategy must first pass the test: will the next holder of power veto it?

C-XZ-001E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-001E.text: Two founding shareholders deadlock over control and the company faces a split; a third-party professional CEO both trust takes interim command, turning 'who swallows whom' into a transition both endorse — settled a year later by an orderly share restructuring.

C-XZ-002E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-002E.text: An industry association's election: two candidates each hold half the board and a vote would split the body; the secretary proposes a third, elder statesman both accept as one transitional president — both candidates stand down, and the next election is held in peace.

C-XZ-003E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-003E.text: The founder surrenders the CEO post and board seat; on great decisions the new management still comes to consult, and he answers never with orders but with questions and cautions — no governance war, influence sustained twenty years.

C-XZ-004E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-004E.text: A retiring university president declines the honorary board seat, accepting only 'come ask whenever needed' — for ten years after, on every major appointment and program decision the new president calls on him privately, and no outsider can name the source of the school's continuity.

C-XZ-005E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-005E.text: A founder-CEO faces the controlling fund's overbearing director: no open clash — transparency and courtesy feed his sense of participation, the charter fences his votes, and after the next round dilutes his stake, control returns in good order.

C-XZ-006E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-006E.text: A veteran vice-president looms over a new president, who does not fight: honors and courtesies in plenty, chairing of grand meetings to set the old man's heart at rest, while the promotions of his subordinates are dispersed across the business lines — the veteran's sway diluted by degrees, and he never feels disfavored.

C-XZ-007E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-007E.text: For ten years the founder stands beside the heir's decisions: never deciding for him, only reviewing and correcting after each major call, teaching in layers from self-mastery to the use of men — at the handover, strategic continuity and the heir's authority both stand.

C-XZ-008E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-008E.text: The grandparents never discipline the grandchild directly; for ten years they call the parents weekly to calibrate the principles of rearing — the child's habits, horizons and way with people bear their imprint, and the grandchild's bond with them is the deepest of all.

C-XZ-009E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-009E.text: Amid a cash crisis and rumors of layoffs, the founder announces purchases of stock at market with personal funds and lends the company his own standby credit line — worth more than any all-hands letter; the panic subsides within a week.

C-XZ-010E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-010E.text: A leaked acquisition crashes the stock and panics the staff; at the emergency meeting the chairman announces a staff stabilization fund backed by a pledge of his own shares — the sum modest, but the news that 'the chairman has staked himself' stops the panic that day.

C-XZ-011E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-011E.text: An old expert with no budget and no headcount has long tended a web across departments — introductions, public backing, free counsel; when transformation demands cross-unit cooperation, only he can bring every key party to one table within a week.

C-XZ-012E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-012E.text: The old secretary-general of an industry association spends his last decade giving free introductions and counsel to every member in trouble — on the day he retires, the joint industry letter he needs is signed overnight by every key name.

C-XZ-013E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-013E.text: A multinational enters a new market: hiring and decisions fully localized, core culture, compliance and financial control never relaxed — calibrated case by case in each clash of local practice and headquarters rule; five years on, neither maladjustment nor loss of control.

C-XZ-014E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-014E.text: A company pushing a global talent strategy simultaneously pledges publicly that headquarters functions will not move and the core team will not be cut — the reform runs unobstructed, because the veterans' security is written explicitly into the plan.

C-XZ-015E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-015E.text: In crisis the CEO first cuts his own pay to the floor and cancels the jet and privileges, then announces the austerity plan for all — because 'I bear it with you' came first, the plan passes the employee council.

C-XZ-016E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-016E.text: A factory relocation burdens the commute; the plant manager is the first to move near the new site and turns his own garage into the shuttle dispatch point — the relocation passes the staff assembly by an overwhelming majority.

C-XZ-017E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-017E.text: Diagnosed with grave illness, the founder triggers the contingency at once: successor, interim council, key mandates and milestones all locked in documents while he is well — half a year later he passes, and the company never spends one day of improvised contest.

C-XZ-018E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-018E.text: The founder names a triumvirate — COO, CFO and a senior outside director — to stand beside the young heir instead of handing all to a single 'number two'; the transition is smooth, with no bid for power.

C-XZ-019E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-019E.text: After positional talks collapse, the opposite side's chief falls ill; the CEO visits the hospital himself and talks of their hometowns and old days — talks reopen a month later: the positions unchanged, the people changed, and terms settled within a week.

C-XZ-020E.civilization: The early Qing court of the Manchu-Mongol conjoint rule: a Khorchin Mongol of the Borjigin wed into the Later Jin khan's house, passing through the reigns of Taizu, Taizong, Shizu and Shengzu, watching a frontier power cross the wall, settle the Central Plain, and turn from conquest to governance — power run on the interweaving of blood, marriage, the banner system and Confucian rite
C-XZ-020E.text: A strike deadlocked for a month, positions irreconcilable; the union leader falls gravely ill and the company's CEO visits the hospital himself and arranges care for the family — when talks resume, the once-immovable term sheet is agreed within three days.

C-LZX-001E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-001E.text: A domestic firm braces for open contest with a global giant; the new strategy head's first act is no counter-strategy but a five-person 'rival research unit': monthly rendering of the rival's earnings calls, patent filings and organizational shifts into an internal bulletin — half a year later every line of the competitive roadmap carries its source.

C-LZX-002E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-002E.text: On the eve of an acquisition, the buyer's team grinds no prices first; it renders the target's charter, past litigation and key executives' public statements into internal cross-reference files — at the table, every clause the seller raises is met with its contradiction to the seller's own precedent.

C-LZX-003E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-003E.text: The quality chief finds a hidden defect in a product batch; a recall will devour the year's profit and offend the whole sales line. He strikes the column 'what it costs me,' weighs only 'the public risk of not recalling,' forces the full recall through and takes the entire accountability before the board — three years on, the reputation built by that recall wins the government contract.

C-LZX-004E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-004E.text: An engineer finds the company's flagship product tainted by data fraud; internal reports sink without a trace. He settles his family, writes his professional testament, then files the whole evidence with the regulator under his own name — dismissed, shut out of the industry, yet two years later the inquiry confirms all, and he sits on the committee revising the standard.

C-LZX-005E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-005E.text: Auditors uncover channel-stuffing fraud through tiers of distributors; the compliance head runs no campaign of wholesale strikes. First he freezes the source accounts of the fraud chain, then requires every distributor to sign a never-again bond and publishes the violators' names — stuffing down nine-tenths in three months, and not one suit lost.

C-LZX-006E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-006E.text: A food company finds a batch of raw material contaminated; the CEO does not quietly rework it — he invites press and customer representatives to witness on site the destruction of the whole stock and publishes the test reports. The stock falls that day, but the witnessed destruction restores the brand within half a year, above its former standing.

C-LZX-007E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-007E.text: While the house still debates whether to learn from the rival, the R&D vice-president has bought three competing units, published the teardowns and raised a benchmarking bench — the debate ends by accomplished fact; the next year the benchmarked product is chartered, and 'learning from the rival' runs from taboo to procedure.

C-LZX-008E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-008E.text: Before leaving, a senior vice-president organizes his accumulated maps of suppliers and notes of technical intelligence into volumes handed to his successor and the company knowledge base — his prelude does not depart with him, but becomes the draft of the firm's three-year catch-up plan.

C-LZX-009E.text: A group launches an anti-bribery drive: first the red-line code with standards, deadlines and consequences published, an amnesty for voluntary disclosure opened, audits started only three months later — four-fifths of historical cases self-report and clear within the amnesty, and the auditors are left only the hard bones.

C-LZX-010E.text: A consignment of hazardous chemicals must be recalled from the market; the regulator weighs and numbers every box, video-records the destruction end to end and publishes the ledger — public doubt of 'a black box' turns into citation of the official ledger, and the disposal passes without a storm.

C-LZX-011E.text: A coastal plant faces typhoon season; the new plant manager issues no exhortation to 'heighten vigilance' but a list — how many generators, how many flood boards, what ceilings for critical stock, who owns which item — and the typhoon leaves the lowest losses on record; the list becomes the group's standard template.

C-LZX-012E.text: After a grave outage, the CTO's postmortem hunts no culprit: he writes the causes as an evidentiary list of what was lacking — no multi-region, no drills, no budget — and the board grants three years of infrastructure spending; the accident becomes the start of the system's upgrade.

C-LZX-013E.text: Headquarters posts a passed-over senior executive to a fringe regional company; he does not wait out his time — he treats the local market as a test field, rebuilding channels, founding a training base, piloting new categories — two years later the region ranks first in growth and his methods are written back into the headquarters manual.

C-LZX-014E.text: An NGO takes over a poor county: no industrial subsidies first — roads, water, power and a vocational school first — three years later the industries come knocking, and 'water before industry' becomes the organization's method of poverty relief.

C-LZX-015E.text: An EV maker hires a foreign team to tune the chassis, but keeps architecture and acceptance in its own chief engineer's hands: deliverables in the contract, the test ground managed by the Chinese side, data kept local — two years on the team graduates, the foreign consultants leave by the terms, and the capability stays in the company.

C-LZX-016E.text: An urban renewal project engages local elders, overseas planners and a university think tank at once, all bound by written statute: who supplies data, who drafts the plan, who accepts it — plural intelligences fitted into one process the city itself holds, and no party grows overmighty.

C-LZX-017E.civilization: The southeastern seaboard and imperial frontier under the Daoguang reign — a closed empire of the cohort-trade system, tribute imagination and draining silver, suddenly colliding with the modern system of treaties, fleets and the world market
C-LZX-017E.text: The house buzzes that 'the rival cannot possibly match our precision'; the R&D director neither believes nor refutes — he buys the rival's unit and sends it to an independent lab. The report shows the rival slightly better; the team overturns its planned route and re-sequences the campaign, sparing strategy from being set by rumor.

C-LZX-018E.text: A research house rules that every conclusion entering the decision meeting must carry source, method and confidence; 'market chatter' is listed apart, never mixed with measured data — two years on its error rate runs well below the industry's, and source-tagging becomes its risk-control signature.

C-LZX-019E.text: At the peak of the company's valuation the founder announces his retreat to technical advisor, handing over to a professional team — the press mourns, the board begs him to stay; he answers 'without desire, strong,' and exits clean — five years later the company rides out the cycle, and the handover is cited as a model of governance.

C-LZX-020E.text: The project succeeds spectacularly; at the celebration the technical lead splits the credit: one-third the team's persistence, one-third the partners', one-third luck — his own name appears only in the list of errors. C-ZZT-002E.text: Thrice failed at the bar, the law graduate abandons the attorney route outright for a legal-tech startup — judging the failures a mismatch of channels rather than a want of effort; three years on, the firm serves a hundred practices.

C-ZZT-003E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-003E.text: After the data breach no one will lead the remediation; a senior architect volunteers: days on the audit, nights on the plan, the work done and a security process standing in three months — half a year later he is formally named head of security.

C-ZZT-004E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-004E.text: The department head leaves and the post stays unfilled; the team's backbone does not grumble but runs the schedule, the meetings and the deliveries 'as acting' — four months on, headquarters ratifies the title upon him.

C-ZZT-006E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-006E.text: A manufacturer locks a fixed share of each year's sales into process retooling, written into the charter rather than approved case by case — through two CEOs and one downturn in five years, the retooling never breaks.

C-ZZT-007E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-007E.text: A SaaS firm faces an aging core product and two new markets at once; the CEO halts all new-market spending and concentrates eighteen months on rewriting the core — the new version steadies the old customers, and the new markets fall two cities deep within six months.

C-ZZT-008E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-008E.text: The chain buys a regional rival and opens no new stores in haste; a year goes to unified supply chain, systems and training — from the second year it expands on the integrated capability, and the unit model outperforms the pre-deal one.

C-ZZT-009E.text: The chip team charters an in-house accelerator: twenty months of architecture validation and toolchain that look like 'no progress'; when the tape-out window opens, design converges in six months and first silicon works — the rival's rushed project is still on its third revision.

C-ZZT-010E.text: A year before the policy opens, the medtech firm has its filings, channel pre-agreements and capacity ready; the week the document issues, the product is on the market and on shelves — two years of preparation compressed into a fortnight's occupation.

C-ZZT-011E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-011E.text: The cross-border e-commerce firm does not run Southeast Asia from headquarters; it moves the product team to Jakarta — local payments, local logistics, local holiday campaigns — and within a year the localized edition outsells the global one.

C-ZZT-012E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-012E.text: Signing its digital-transformation contract, the automaker writes in: within three years the joint team delivers the system and trains thirty in-house engineers, the consultants to exit at term — in the fourth year no renewal, the capability stays.

C-ZZT-013E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame

C-ZZT-016E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-016E.text: Before the mountain, the expedition assembles satellite imagery, hydrology and herders' interviews into a route model, correcting assumptions daily on the march — the plan diverts where measured melt says it must, and the team misses the collapse that follows on the old line.

C-ZZT-017E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-017E.text: The CTO and the sales VP clash over taking a big client's customization order; the CTO does not fight it out in the meeting but files a written analysis — capacity figures, delivery risk, opportunity cost — and the CEO rules on the data; the quarrel ends in three days.

C-ZZT-018E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-018E.text: Two partners break privately over equity, yet outwardly sign jointly and divide work by the company's rules — clients and staff sense nothing, and the valuation never wobbles.

C-ZZT-019E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-019E.text: The day the listing closes, the founder calls a family meeting and sets three house rules: the children's schooling by merit, not by a donated building; family spending on its own budget; no relatives in the company — ten years on, the succession is smooth and the family without scandal.

C-ZZT-020E.civilization: The late Qing in its double crisis — the Taiping and the northwest rebellions tearing the empire, the sea coast and the frontier alarming at once, the Hunan Army's provincial finance and the self-strengthening of the foreign-learnings rising together inside one decaying frame
C-ZZT-020E.text: Before retiring, the entrepreneur gives most of the fortune to a foundation, leaving the children an education fund and one sentence: 'come to me with a business plan' — twenty years on, both children run companies of their own, and the foundation still funds the field's research.

C-GSJ-001E.civilization: The astronomical-calendrical and hydraulic scene of the Yuan dynasty: born in 1231 at Xingtai in Xingzhou (today's Hebei) — his grandfather Guo Rong was versed in the classics, mathematics and waterworks, and the boy learned first from him, then from Liu Bingzhong (the Zijinshan school), with Wang Xun a fellow student; at fifteen or sixteen he obtained a diagram of the 'lotus-flower clepsydra' and 'had fully exhausted its principle', building from bamboo strips a gnomon ring and an earthen platform for observing; in 1262, recommended by Zhang Wenqian, he stood before Kublai Khan and laid out six proposals for waterworks, and was at once made Commissioner of Canals for all circuits; in 1264 he went with Zhang Wenqian to the Tangut lands, 'renewing along the old lines and setting new sluices', restoring the Tanglai, Hanyan and a dozen more ancient canals with sixty-odd branch channels, irrigating over ninety thousand hectares; thereafter he surveyed the Ordos reaches of the Yellow River and reopened the Jinzhou Canal — with a pre-cut spillway to avert floods, it served nearly thirty years; in 1276 he was charged, with Wang Xun and Xu Heng, to make a new calendar, advancing the principle that 'the root of the calendar is in measurement, and for measurement no tool comes before gnomon and sphere' — he built or rebuilt nearly twenty instruments, among them the abridged armilla, the high gnomon, the shadow-definer (jingfu), the horizon bowl-dial, the star-peeker, the pole-observer, the lattice instrument and the orientation board; in 1279 he directed the 'Survey of the Four Seas' — 'east to Koryo, west to the Dianchi lake, south past the red cliffs of Hainan, north to the Iron Le', at twenty-seven stations; the gnomon tower at Dengfeng with its 'sky-measuring scale' stands to this day; in 1280 the Shoushi calendar was completed, promulgated in 1281 — the tropical year at 365.2425 days, the same value as the Gregorian reform three centuries later, discarding the fictitious 'grand epoch', inventing cubic interpolation and the arc-sagitta conversion; it ran for more than 360 years, the longest-lived of Chinese calendars; in 1291 he returned as Director of Waterways and built the Tonghui Canal — leading the Baifu spring west around Kunming Lake into the capital, solving Dadu's water supply, with twenty-four gates and weirs to hold the level, so that grain barges from the south sailed straight into Jishuitan; and he once 'compared the levels of the capital and Bianliang against the sea surface' — the earliest recorded sea-level datum, the concept of altitude above sea level; in old age he directed the Tiebanquan channel at Shangdu: the builders altered his design, and the flood destroyed the channel — hence the saying that 'Master Guo is not to be matched'; he died in office in 1316, aged eighty-six; a lunar crater (1970) and asteroid 2012 (1977) bear his name, and Johann Schreck's successor-eulogist Johann Adam Schall called him 'the Tycho of China' — the great integrator of instrument, observation, calculation and waterworks in Chinese science history.
C-GSJ-001E.text: A company's pricing committee had argued for two months over whether to raise prices: marketing brought competitor screenshots, finance brought margin models, sales brought customer threats — every side reasoning, no one holding new data; the new CPO called off the meeting with one question: 'what data does this decision need, and how much of it do we have?' The inventory showed the deficit was not argument but three crucial customer interviews and a true distribution of closed-deal prices — 'measure first, argue after', she said: in two weeks two hundred genuine transaction samples were collected and cleaned, and once the price-band distribution appeared, marketing's and finance's arguments were simultaneously demoted to 'two readings of the same distribution'; the meeting shifted from 'who persuades whom' to 'which segment of the distribution is still missing'; pricing was finally set at the distribution's 75th percentile and no one cited a screenshot again — the rule she left the team: 'any topic argued twice without result — first check whether the data suffice; if not, go measure; only after measuring may the arguing resume.'

C-GSJ-002E.text: A coffee chain's operations manual had grown to four hundred pages in twenty years: every page had once earned its place in some incident, and so all remained — new store managers took six weeks of training and still could not master the manual, while surprise-inspection pass rates fell year by year; the new operations director did not add a page but held the manual to account, line by line: every clause had to answer 'which real failure does it pay for?' — after a two-week audit, 173 clauses were flagged as ceremonial (written as risk-avoidance, now pure interference) and deleted at a stroke; training shrank from six weeks to three, and inspection pass rates rose four points — at the review she said: 'rings are what a thousand years only adds; each was justified when added, yet rings block the star you want to see. What we deleted was not the rules but the occlusions between them.'

C-GSJ-003E.text: A factory's dimensional-inspection tolerance chronically missed spec, and the QC team's three upgrades of calipers and optical magnification changed nothing; the new process engineer stopped looking at the inspection end and walked upstream toward the error's birthplace: the bulk of the drift came from the die temperature's daily fluctuation — a tenfold finer instrument would only measure a drifting quantity precisely; he installed a fifteen-hundred-dollar closed-loop die-temperature controller and the drift vanished at its source — not one inspection device replaced, yield within tolerance rose from 83% to 99.2%; in his report he wrote: 'refinement at the reading end polishes bookkeeping; structure at the source repairs the thing itself — repair the thing, then the books.'

C-CY-001E.title_en: Seeking Truth from Facts — Economic System Reform Direction Judgment Case
C-CY-001E.description_en: During the early reform and opening-up period, facing debates between planned economy and market economy, Chen Yun insisted on making practical judgments based on actual conditions, proposing 'planned economy as the mainstay with market regulation as supplementary', maintaining socialist direction while acknowledging market role.

C-CY-002E.title_en: Investigation and Research — Rural Reform Policy Formulation Case
C-CY-002E.description_en: Before implementing the household responsibility system, Chen Yun conducted in-depth field investigations of Xiaogang Village's practical results in Anhui Province, proposing policy recommendations supporting rural reform based on field survey data.

C-CY-003E.description_en: When making major reform decisions, Chen Yun adhered to the 'exchange-compare-repeated' method: broadly soliciting opinions from all sides (exchange), comparing pros and cons of multiple plans (compare), forming final decisions after repeated deliberation (repeated).

C-CY-004E.title_en: Crossing the River by Feeling Stones — Gradual Reform Case
C-CY-004E.description_en: During China's transition from rural to urban reform, Chen Yun advocated a gradual strategy: first piloting the household responsibility system in small rural areas, then gradually expanding to urban economic sectors after successful results.

C-CY-005E.title_en: Comprehensive Balance — National Economy Proportion Coordination Case
C-CY-005E.description_en: During the 'First Five-Year Plan', Chen Yun emphasized coordinating proportions among agriculture, light industry and heavy industry, opposing unbalanced development that pursued heavy industry at the expense of agriculture and light industry.

C-CY-006E.title_en: Planned-Market Unity — Dual-Track Price System Exploration Case
C-CY-006E.description_en: During China's transition from planned to market economy, Chen Yun proposed 'planned as mainstay, market as supplementary' dual-track thinking: important materials subject to planned prices, general goods allowed market regulation.

C-CY-007E.title_en: Key Breakthrough and Comprehensive Balance — Industrial Structure Adjustment Case
C-CY-007E.description_en: In the early reform period, Chen Yun proposed focusing on agriculture and energy/transportation as two key breakthroughs while balancing coordinated development across industry, light industry and other sectors.

C-CY-008E.title_en: Stability First — Economic Overheating Control Case
C-CY-008E.description_en: When the economy experienced overheating in the mid-1980s, Chen Yun adhered to stability-first principles, advocating control of investment scale and compression of basic construction while maintaining reform momentum.

C-CY-009E.title_en: Practice as Criterion — Reform Policy Effectiveness Assessment Case
C-CY-009E.description_en: For every economic policy, Chen Yun insisted on testing through practical results: Shenzhen SEZ success, township enterprise rise, and foreign investment effectiveness were all verified by actual development data.

C-CY-010E.title_en: Act According to Capability — Infrastructure Investment Scale Decision Case
C-CY-010E.description_en: In discussions of major projects like 'South-to-North Water Diversion', Chen Yun insisted on acting according to national capacity: first assessing fiscal capability and resource endowment before determining reasonable investment scale and construction pace.

C-JX-001E.title_en: "Horizontal Transplantation" — Cross-Cultural Borrowing in Taiwan's Modern Poetry Movement
C-JX-001E.description_en: In the 1950s, Ji Xian proposed his 'horizontal transplantation' theory in Taiwan's poetry scene, advocating direct learning from Western modernist poets (Baudelaire, Rimbaud, Eliot) rather than following the longitudinal lineage of traditional Chinese poetics. This concept, promoted through his Modern Poetry quarterly, fundamentally changed the direction of Taiwanese poetry and became a milestone in the history of Chinese-language modern poetry.

C-JX-002E.title_en: "Emphasis on Intellectuality" — The Dominant Role of Rational Reflection in Poetry Creation
C-JX-002E.description_en: Ji Xian explicitly stated in his six commandments that 'new poetry is the emphasis on intellectuality,' arguing that poetry should not rely solely on emotional lyricism but should incorporate rational reflection and intellectual thought. This is embodied in works like 'Your Name,' where gentle language conceals philosophical depth about existence, memory, and emotional resonance.

C-JX-003E.title_en: "Pure Poetry" — Ontological Distinction Between Poetry and Prose
C-JX-003E.description_en: Ji Xian asserted that 'modern poetry is pure poetry, distinct from prose-poetry,' emphasizing poetry's independent ontological value and aesthetic autonomy. This theoretical stance liberated Taiwanese modern poetry from traditional lyricism, shifting toward pure exploration of language, form, and imagery, influencing subsequent generations of Taiwanese poets.

C-JX-004E.title_en: Existentialist Poetics — Philosophical Resources in Modern Poetry
C-JX-004E.description_en: Ji Xian argued that existentialism is a crucial source of modern poetry, introducing Sartre and Camus's philosophical ideas into poetic creation. His poems often use the 'lone wolf' metaphor, expressing individual loneliness, freedom, and resistance — transforming existentialist reflections on the human condition into profound poetic expression.

C-JX-005E.title_en: "Poetry as Humanity's Elevated Part" — Theoretical Construction of Poetry's Transcendent Value
C-JX-005E.description_en: In his six commandments, Ji Xian proposed that 'poetry is the elevated part of human life,' asserting that poetry should transcend everyday experience and reach spiritual elevation. This theory established a lofty value position for Taiwanese modern poetry, making poetry the vehicle of human spiritual freedom.

C-JX-006E.title_en: "Six Commandments" — Systematic Construction of Modern Poetic Theory
C-JX-006E.description_en: Ji Xian systematically proposed six commandments in Modern Poetry: horizontal transplantation, emphasis on intellectuality, pure poetry, existentialist source, elevated part, and new humanity. These six commandments formed a complete modern poetic theory system — from methodology (horizontal transplantation) to ontology (pure poetry) and axiology (elevated part) — providing a systematic theoretical framework for Taiwanese modern poetry.

C-JX-007E.title_en: "Lone Wolf" Spirit — The Artistic Persona of Solitary Independence
C-JX-007E.description_en: Ji Xian frequently identified himself as a 'lone wolf' in his poems, expressing an artistic persona that refused to conform and stood independent of crowds. Rejecting group-style creative models, he insisted on individual perspective and unique expression. This 'lone wolf' spirit became a spiritual symbol of Taiwan's modern poetry scene, influencing countless young poets pursuing artistic independence.

C-JX-008E.title_en: Blue Star Debate — Modern Poetry Route Controversy Case
C-JX-008E.description_en: Ji Xian's debates with the Blue Star Poetry Society (Qin Zihao, Yu Guangzhong et al.) were pivotal events in Taiwan's modern poetry history. Blue Star advocated 'lyrical tradition' and 'national spirit,' opposing Ji's 'horizontal transplantation.' This debate promoted Taiwan modern poetry's多元化 (diversity), deepening poetic creation through clashing philosophies.

C-JX-009E.title_en: "New Humanity" — Poetry's Value Orientation Toward Modern People
C-JX-009E.description_en: In his sixth commandment, Ji Xian declared that 'new poetry must belong to new humanity (modern humans),' advocating that poetry should address modern society's people and their existential circumstances. This shifted Taiwanese modern poetry from classical lyricism toward attention to modern humans' spiritual conditions, infusing poetry with contemporary relevance and realistic concern.

C-JX-010E.title_en: Lifelong Creative Practice — Validating Poetic Theory Through Continuous Creation
C-JX-010E.description_en: From his active years in 1930s Shanghai literary circles, to founding Modern Poetry quarterly in Taiwan (1953), and continuing creative output into old age (including 'Fifty at Ninety' published at age 90), Ji Xian validated his poetic theory through nearly a century of continuous creative practice. Even at 90, he maintained active thinking and rich imagination — 'still very beautiful' — setting an example of lifelong creative dedication.

C-SAD-001E.civilization: Egypt and the Middle East at the turning point of the 1970s: between a poor Delta village and the Royal Military Academy in Cairo — the intellectual soldier who heard elders tell anti-British stories in childhood and read and meditated alone through four and a half years in prison; conspirator and prisoner of the Nasser revolution — a core member of the Free Officers of 1952 and the voice that announced the revolution on the radio, yet twice (1946, and after 1952 political disgrace) jailed and marginalised; the catastrophe of the 1967 Six-Day War and Nasser's death lifting him to the presidency — a nation supposing him a mere caretaker while he quietly purged the pyramid of power as the 'loyal colonel'; Soviet arms and advisers at remote control, Kissinger's diplomacy giving Egypt the cold shoulder, the stalemate of 'no war, no peace' of 1971-1973 — within which he made the decision to lever unlimited diplomacy with a limited war; the October crossing and the new Egyptian self-confidence, the debut of the oil weapon, and the 1977 journey to Jerusalem and Camp David — his historical position completed at once by the peace treaty and by assassination
C-SAD-001E.text: A company has 'leaked early' before every launch for five years without ever shipping on schedule, until media and rivals default to wolf-cry; the new product head turns the record around: the real redesign completed in silence, unsealed only on launch day — the rival's intelligence files the conclusive supply-chain evidence as one more cry of wolf, and the response window is eaten whole.

C-SAD-002E.civilization: Egypt and the Middle East at the turning point of the 1970s: between a poor Delta village and the Royal Military Academy in Cairo — the intellectual soldier who heard elders tell anti-British stories in childhood and read and meditated alone through four and a half years in prison; conspirator and prisoner of the Nasser revolution — a core member of the Free Officers of 1952 and the voice that announced the revolution on the radio, yet twice (1946, and after 1952 political disgrace) jailed and marginalised; the catastrophe of the 1967 Six-Day War and Nasser's death lifting him to the presidency — a nation supposing him a mere caretaker while he quietly purged the pyramid of power as the 'loyal colonel'; Soviet arms and advisers at remote control, Kissinger's diplomacy giving Egypt the cold shoulder, the stalemate of 'no war, no peace' of 1971-1973 — within which he made the decision to lever unlimited diplomacy with a limited war; the October crossing and the new Egyptian self-confidence, the debut of the oil weapon, and the 1977 journey to Jerusalem and Camp David — his historical position completed at once by the peace treaty and by assassination
C-SAD-002E.text: The industry number two, knowing the frontal war unwinnable against the leader, fights a local campaign 'only to prove it can hurt': all resources concentrated on a tenfold experience of the leader's most profitable SKU; three months later the leader's board invites it to the standards table for the first time — the campaign closed at its crest and the transition into negotiation made.

C-SAD-003E.text: A parachuted executive dorms in a faction-ridden company under the persona of the proceduralist: pledging every process, keeping all the old ministers, quietly building a dossier per person; when one faction strikes first and is caught doctoring appraisal data, he reconstitutes management overnight in the name of lawful correction — the whole cost of the purge borne by the party that moved first.

C-SAD-004E.civilization: Egypt and the Middle East at the turning point of the 1970s: between a poor Delta village and the Royal Military Academy in Cairo — the intellectual soldier who heard elders tell anti-British stories in childhood and read and meditated alone through four and a half years in prison; conspirator and prisoner of the Nasser revolution — a core member of the Free Officers of 1952 and the voice that announced the revolution on the radio, yet twice (1946, and after 1952 political disgrace) jailed and marginalised; the catastrophe of the 1967 Six-Day War and Nasser's death lifting him to the presidency — a nation supposing him a mere caretaker while he quietly purged the pyramid of power as the 'loyal colonel'; Soviet arms and advisers at remote control, Kissinger's diplomacy giving Egypt the cold shoulder, the stalemate of 'no war, no peace' of 1971-1973 — within which he made the decision to lever unlimited diplomacy with a limited war; the October crossing and the new Egyptian self-confidence, the debut of the oil weapon, and the 1977 journey to Jerusalem and Camp David — his historical position completed at once by the peace treaty and by assassination
C-SAD-004E.text: A factory's 'unrebuildable' old line is re-translated by a newcomer: the so-called bottleneck is mere loose sand, washable by a 'flow of information' — a kanban system re-routes the process rhythm, and six hours open a blockage three years had failed to open; 'insurmountable' was only a variable no one had changed.
